I like the simpler earlier version in which you can do solo with boss or needed a fewer people to raid the 5-star boss. Or you can collect things randomly from wherever you go. Now, it is more of everything, puzzle, accumulate skills, collect items, making quests. Popularity of the game will plunge down.

Just rejoined after deleting it two years ago and there have been a lot of upgrades! More Poke Stops and gyms, which is nice. However, the two-star rating is for the distance tracker and Adventure Sync. If the main point of this game is motivate people moving, then the trackers shouldn't be as off as they are. We walked at least a mile last night with the Adventure Sync on and full battery use, yet nothing was tracked in the game. Even checked this morning to see no progress added.

This game was everything I have hoped for since I was a child. My wife and I would go for regular walks because the adventurer in us was given tools of the hunt. Namely a decent tracking feature with the foot prints. It was fun hunting them down with that as our guide. Now there is... whatever this is. I rarely see people out wandering about. And neither my wife or I even bother to open the game. I miss what it was and could still be.

I originally left a 5 star review, but recent changes in the game took away features that made the game more enjoyable. Also increasing prices for events that are lackluster and not releasing details of "boosted" rates has been misleading and poorly executed. Niantic created a supposed task force to listen to their players but that was quickly taken away and the game is headed in the wrong direction. I have played since the games launch as well.

The lag during battles is beyond frustrating. Frequently, the charged attack buttons don't show up when you change Pokémon until your opponent has already hit theirs. Battles also will just freeze, and the only way to do anything is to quit the battle. It's incredibly frustrating, especially with the battle limit. I've experienced this on various different wifi connections and on phone data. Sometimes, when you change your battle party, it will put your previous battle party in the battle

I hadn't played in a while so I figured I'd download it again. Now I remember why I stopped playing to begin with. Simple things like potions, which used to spawn with a frequency that made the game playable, are so uncommon now it's practically unplayable. I genuinely used to love playing Pokemon go, but now it's nothing more than a cash grab scheme designed to nickel and dime it's players in hopes of any kind of progression. Oh, and $15 for community day? Get wrecked.

Used to be a great game. And while there were always extras you could buy, the game was still mostly free. But it's gotten less & less so. There's some pokemon you just can't get unless you buy a ticket for it. Having major glitches seems to be a weekly thing now. I just bought a whole bunch of coins right before the announcement, but when they are used up, I think I will leave the game. Maybe these coins will last me until my 7 year anniversary.

The game itself is fun however there are still glitches that make the game unplayable from time to time. They've ruined battles at gyms for the casual player by making potions basically impossible to get. So you end up stuck with 30 dead Pokemon at a time. They've finally added in trading and a few other things that should have been included at launch really. Niantic had really played the customer well by making them pay to get essential items for the game to continue. Overall it really is a good game but it's become one of those 5-10 minutes at a time games like clash. I've uninstalled several times already and eventually it'll meet the same fate as clash.

EDIT: I've since started playing again and with the addition of trainer battles and trades, rocket stops, and buddy Pokemon, the game has vastly improved. I'd still like to see some updates to reduce bugs and make the overall user experience a bit smoother, but it's definitely better than it used to be. This game is arguably the most overhyped and underwhelming game I've downloaded. It promises a Pokémon adventure, yet it has nothing that made the Pokémon games great.

I used to love playing this game but stopped playing because I couldn't rationalize getting my young son out in crazy temperatures. I was able to start playing again when they made changes to the stop radius. But now it's very disappointing that Niantic changed it back in the middle of a pandemic and won't be able to play again. Do better Niantic.

This game is designed to waste away your time. You try to catch something valuable, you have to get through annoyingly long ball wiggle animations, pokémon breaks free despite ultraball/spinning/great throw, and after 4th try, runs away. Then all the pop-up menus, checking IVs, hidden level, feeding companion could be 10 times faster, so I can't use it while being out in the city.

Game is ok. They focus too much on trying to make money and less on what the player base would like to have. Also increasing the price of an already fictional item that doesn't actually have value is a garbage move. If you want to be better people try instead to create a new item that has value that people would be willing to buy rather than raising prices. Never will play again.

Won't work one Google Pixel. Was able to set up my account but as soon as I was required to catch a Pokemon, I wasn't able. GPS error even with my location turned on, restarting the app, and the device. Worked fine on my old iPhone. Really disappointed because I would have loved to keep playing. Edit: It has worked for the past couple months!

Really good game, but I can't do much where I am due to the lack of other players in this area, making it virtually impossible so continue, not only this but raising the prices of everything in the item shop is just ridiculous, the remote raid passes in particular, I feel 150 or 120 would be better than 195. However, when you have other players, it is very fun. One thing though, is it crashes way too much

I gotta say I love this game. the visuals are stunning, the Pokémon are amazing, but some of the mechanics are wonky. the tracker that tracks how far you've walked could use some work, especially with the eggs, and they only limited the Pokémon to being able to use two moves, a base move and then a special move. the worst part of that is that you can't keep moves and still learn new ones at the same time.

I liked the original Pokémon tracker with the footprints and pings, even with those aspects helping the player it was still hard to find Pokémon, but it wasn't hard enough to make it not fun. Now it's close to impossible to find a Pokémon you have your eye on. I don't like the no footprints idea. Also with the new update it takes forever for Pokéstops and gyms to load after opening the game and seeing the map. When they do finally pop up I can't even collect my rewards. Needs work.

I started out playing this game with high hopes, as a Pokemon fan from the beginning. After nearly a year I dropped it due to lack of non-bug-related updates. I'm very glad I picked it up again a couple of years later. There are now an abundance of Pokemon and more are released on a regular basis. The addition of quests that allow you to add myths and raids for legends only increases the fun. The downsides;. Heavily biased to cities/ downtown, can get laggy.

Been playing for years now and while I still love the game, all the quality of life changes made during covid were so helpful for people like myself who lived in areas it wasn't safe to walk but I have to take away a few points due to them undoing them. Not to mention some of the missions are getting way to hard for people in areas with no gyms to complete which only furthers the need for more ease of access to raids/pokestops.

I, like many others, am very disappointed in the recent changes in the game. Those complaints have already been enumerated by many others. It seems, though, that the game is now very difficult to load and freezes in the middle of play, battling, or doing a raid (when raiding is actually possible). Too bad cuz I was really enjoying the game.

Its a great game. but i would like an addition to the game where we can actually see other players on our screen as well. that way we can add friends easily or even battle them easily. scanning the qr code is good and all but its wierd to search for more friends by checking their screen to see if they are playing the game or not ( this app isnt as popular in my country ).

The game appears to have a very simple architecture so it should run fairly smoothly on newer devices, & In concept the game is enjoyable. On the few times that it works for more than 15 minutes it's fun. But this game crashes more than any game I've ever tried to play. So you finally catch that Pokemon you've been looking for you give it raspberries and use 5 Ultra Balls, then your game freezes and when you turn back on the Pokemon is gone never reappears and all of your balls are gone.

The first couple of days of the game, worked like a charm. Then the after the servers crashed all hell broke loose. The GPS won't work except for 10 seconds if I'm lucky. Edit!!! Game works much better now. I can catch pokemon, it reads my steps, do battles and trades. Fight in Gym and Raids. The only downside is sometimes it randomly exits the game but doesn't happen all that much.

Awesome game love it! Play it EVERY day! Took a star away for each of two reasons: 1) the 50 coin per day max is totally a rip off! If you put mons in gyms you should be entitled to the coins, regardless of if they all return the same day or not. 2) the "online" friends list is never working properly. You still end up having to scan your friends list to find online players because it doesn't correctly sort them all to the top of the list as it should. Should even be able to do it in real-time.

As of 1/2020 after not playing for a year, the game improved considerably. New areas, evolution stones, trainer battling, trading, best friends, research, and buddy walking has made the game much more involved and enjoyable. There are still issues with raids most recently, during gofest 2021, the game froze while trying to catch one of the legendary Pokemon. The event was disappointing, but it was a great way to build up stardust.

Since the update I can't can't use properly cause the GPS keeps moving me to areas that I'm not in. It keeps jumping from scene to scene without me being there. Bug needs to be fixed. Also this app keeps saying GPS not found. I have tried everything! Now that you have added the trainer vs trainer battles the game frequently freezes! How do you add something but it makes it worse!

From great to garbage. Whatever this new update is, I am sure it is terrific, but I can no longer play the game. The game starts to load, then crashes. Several attempts at proper tech support have yielded nothing. I cannot load into the game to ask from there, so all of my time and effort playing was for nothing. Deleting the app. Cheers Niantic, on making a once wonderful game deletable.

I really love the game. I do. But having to click this stupid "You're moving too fast" button every five minutes while im riding with my parents, is just ridiculously irritating. I live in a mostly unsafe area, and not being able to pick up pokestops while im riding in a car is ridiculous. There are loads of people that are completely incapable of playing properly because they cant walk at glacial shift speed to pick up each one. People will ALWAYS play while driving. Stop hindering gameplay.

I honestly was hoping to fall in love with this app but it is constantly crashing. It doesn't keep track of the distance I have traveled just to hatch an egg. I catch a Pokémon and all the sudden it crashes and the Pokémon is gone along with the Pokéball. This is just a couple of the issues I have came across out of the 9 I have written down. I will revise my review once the app is fixed or if it gets fixed before I move on and forget about it. Much better than it was!

Gameplay has improved. Newer features are nice but attention span seems to be shortlived. What happens when you run out of Pokémon to introduce? Still several years down the line, at which point in sure a new game will be introduced. Gym mechanics still sketchy, however raids help promote multiplayer. Sad that there is no room in the meta for lower stat mons. I left awhile back. Periodically jump on here and there, but would not call myself the full-time player I used to be.

Pros: it's addictive and fun. Cons: errors. No reimbursement when error out of gym raids even if I used my premium pass. Still waiting to hear back from Niantic from the first time this happened to me and I submitted a complaint over a month ago. They don't take their customers seriously and they never reimburse when they are at fault. I will edit this review as I see fit.

I love Pokemon GO. The ability to catch pokemon in AR is amazing, I had started playing years ago but stopped. My husband got me back into it during Covid and it was AMAZING! All of the changes made playing easier for me after just having a baby and myself not being able to go out in the heat often. But now they reversed the changes and I can't play anymore...I can't leave my house to play...so it was a good game, but I can't recommend it anymore.

Fantastic game and I absolutely love playing it. It's given me a good reason to go out and see new places in my hometown, and its nostalgic feeling like a real life Pokemon trainer lol. Wish they would do some work on improving the frame rate of the game and glitchy behavior when things get busy but at the same time its sort of expected. I wish incences were a little more effective and if anything could be multiplied by nearby people using them as well if you're friends. Keep it up though!!(:

I've played this game for years off and on. Each time it's been better than before, but for some reason as of the last few updates, the game has become unbearably laggy. It has reached a point where it is borderline unplayable. I have adjusted all the in game settings and my phone settings, but it's still extremely slow. I've burned so many pokeballs and resources just trying to throw them or attack, but because of the lag you completely miss, or your pokemon faints because it didn't register.

I know for a fact adventure sync worked for me when it first came out. I was excited when I discovered the game didn't even need to be running in the background or have data turned on as long as location was on. Today I had to rush somewhere (less than 12 mph on a bike) at about 3 mile roundtrip. Checked my egg before I started .65 km. Checked it afterwards. .65km. No buddy distance either. When I looked into it it's mentioned you should try having "Google Fit" turned on. Never had it on before.

Original review: Let's face it, we've been waiting for this for our entire lives! Then the devs stopped the game from working. I got to level 19 in a week, and have been unable to get past 21 in the next fortnight. Thanks devs!!! Suburban gameplay is literally impossible Updated review (2018>: after a long hiatus, I'm back in and it's great fun. I still miss the original tracking system, and I still think suburban gameplay sucks (let alone rural), but having moved into a denser region, and with more than two pokestops nearby, it's actually playable again, and great fun

It used to be a good game. Now, the prices have literally doubled for in-game purchases, which legitimately make the game almost unplayable and not enjoyable anymore. At the same time, the content in the game has become very lackluster, uneventful, unrewarding, and very boring. The overall experience from this game is pretty much ruined now since it requires players to rely on buying newly overpriced ingame items to even try to manage to get together and succeed in what the developers intended.

I literally love this game and have played it consistently since 2016. Unfortunately, it turns out you can accidentally transfer Cosmog, making it so that you can't complete all the quests without Cosmog and you only ever get one in the game (and yet it's transferable?? A required Pokemon that you will NEVER see again is transferrable). I was told I might as well delete the game after that mistake, so I reached out to support. Turns out I might as well delete the game -_- real waste of 7 years.

I really liked this game when I first started playing it. It's fun, gets you out of the house, and is a great way to meet new people but the glitchiness and constant freezing have me fed up. I hate when I catch a good pokemon the game freezes so I lose poke balls and don't even get to keep the monster. Nintendo and the other company need to get on top of this ASAP at least give us the pokeballs we lose and the monsters we've caught. Not playing it till it gets fixed.

I've been playing since 2016 and the game was a childhood dream come true for me when it first launched. Unfortunately Niantic seems to be bent on sabotaging themselves and is limiting the game to essentially able-bodied, driving urban players (and bonus points if they have money to burn). As a non-driving student living in a dangerous city, making progress in this game is incredibly difficult, and participating in events is even more so. Seeing this game go downhill the way is has is very sad.

Have played off and on since launch. Don't have much free time to play the way they want you to play, and it feels like I accomplish less and less with what time I do spend on game. I'm in the suburbs of a major city, so the lack of spawns and gyms is disappointing. At some point in the last year, the game now demands I relogin every time I launch the game. Overall, the game is a disappointment, both as a Pokemon game, and as a mobile game.

Overall the game is fun so long as you have poke balls and people to play with. That being said the games GPS and it's tracking sometimes fail, and don't track well. As of this last update I haven't been able to log on and the teams support on the subject is null. And I've looked to see if anyone else was having the issue or had a solution and come up with nothing I haven't already tried.

Love catching Pokémon, but the battle system is TERRIBLE. Connection issues are poor regardless of where I am, whether I'm using WiFi or data, doesn't even matter if I use a different device. Connectivity is almost always poor. I'll lose a battle that's super even all because the game will lag and won't register me tapping the special attack, even if I hit it TEN TIMES IN A ROW. Very frustrating to be beaten in a dishonorable way.

It's an amazing game that encourage you to explore places you haven't thought of visiting and make new friends. But it's also about pure luck. You could be spending time, money, energy, & battery life grinding, battling and other stuff yet still left frustrated with the results. While other players just take less effort and get way better pokemons. That is so not fair!

Poke Go's gameplay is shallow, but good enough to be worth playing socially. I wish raids weren't prohibitively hard for smaller groups of people, since a lot of Pokemon are locked behind them. Similarly there's little reason to catch the majority of Pokemon other than for the sake of collecting, as very few are useful in raids, and gym battles are easy enough not to worry. Even most legendaries aren't worth using unless you dump a load of rare candy into leveling them up to par with what you already have. My real issue comes from the bugginess of the game. I haven't been able to play consistently for the last six months without the game 'failing to log in', for days on end. I've found the only way to fix this near daily issue is to clear the cache, log out, and log back in, having to reset my settings each time. This is ridiculous, and makes it near impossible to have fun playing. Ruined the last few community days and wasted lucky eggs, until I just stopped trying to play.

Still keeping a 4 star, but now for a different reason. This game has improved so much since I last played. It's incredible and I find it insane that this is finally a game I *really* enjoy playing. You all have made incredible progress. Right now, honestly my only two problems are as follows: First, I hate that my Pokemon could get locked in a gym forever and get no benefit. Please at least allow the Pokemon to return with items if you hit the 50 coin limit. Second, *please* let us discard eggs

After playing the game since release there have been many changes within the game. especially regarding prices for certain items. This has been a constant battle to keep items more "affordable" for people rather than outrageously expensive, and it seems with the most recent update Niantic is doubling down on this. They are not adjusting prices for the most bought items used by players so they can make more money but label it as a "rebalance" for the item. Now encouraging you more to spend money.

Good game if you're a pokemon fan, otherwise I'd be less confident recommending it. The game is somewhat past it's prime, both in terms of popularity (summer 2016) and ideal player experience (the company is actively rolling back improvements made during 2020 which aid rural and remote play because they can't sell as much data if you have to walk around less). It's still enjoyable if you did enjoy it in it's prime, but I don't know a lot of people who have stuck with it.

I love Pokémon and I think this game was fun, but server issues and a few glitches kept it from being perfect. Then they shut the tracking system down and still haven't even bothered to fix the original bugs. Basically, the only way to catch a Pokémon is to wander around aimlessly until your phone vibrates. With the most recent update, the game has pretty much become a glorified pedometer.

The new update to the player characters is just bad to look at. While the old models didn't have the same customization options, I see no reason why they had to be completely scrapped rather than expanded upon. Beyond the wierdly realistic/detailed features and the unappealing and derpy looking faces, the new models just don't look good. They don't even carry the same artstyle as the rest of the human characters, making their appearance much more of an eyesore.

You finally confirmed in your policy update that you're crawling through our phones & gathering a list of installed apps. You claim it's to prevent cheating which is possible, but I don't recall being prompted to allow you to do this. It's an invasion of my device & privacy. You need to be more open about what data you're downloading from our phones. Why does PoGo freeze any time I connect or disconnect a Bluetooth headset? It happens with everyone I own. Are you parsing external devices too?

Been playing since 2016 and they've recently decided on changing the range of pokestops to a reduced range. Niantic wants people to go out and explore the world but since the range of stops are reduced, it's hard to go to some areas without trespassing. Also, there are many times where the pokestops are across the street. Before this change, I was able to reach it without causing danger to myself from having to go across the lanes.

Lots of fun! very addictive! i love that team rocket has joined the game!!! I wish we could trade with friends without having to sit right next to them. I'll be moving soon and won't be able to trade pokemon with friends that I leave behind. It would also be nice if we could trade items instead of deleting ones we dont need. It seems really wasteful.

The concept is great, it was a massive hit and even gained news coverage. And yeah, going out to capture pokemon can actually be fun. But the problems? You can't fight with friends at your own leisure. You cant , say visit a friend's house and have just a short, friendly match. The only way you can fight are through gyms which is tedious. Plus you need data to play the game, if you don't have data then you can't progress whatsoever, which is off-putting for many, including me

Raising the star level, was playing the game when it first came out and plagued with issues. Majority of those issues have been resolved and the game is much better. There is now a lot more to do, trading, team rocket battles, raiding, etc. The problem i have now is the RNG. It just feels that the RNG is not in my favor so i feel like i am missing out on some of the rare stuff.

New features such as adventure sync do not work for me. I have tried keeping pokemon go on in background, on with screen off, and syncing Google fit to pokemon go. Despite racking up nearly 200 km a week on google fit, and settings saying that it is connected to pokemon go, I havent gotten a single adventure sync km. I rarely play now because new features are impossible for me. I'm looking forward to trainer battles but maybe they wont go as expected either. My last problem is that there aren't many pokemon go players around me so it's nearly impossible to catch a legendary in battle. Other than that, graphics are nice and the game isn't as glitchy as it was in release so it can still be a fun play. Plus there are loads of new pokemon to catch... maybe there are more pokemon than you get storage space for your character though which would mean a mandatory purchase for a storage upgrade. It's kind of hard to get lots of in game coins unless you play a lot or use real money.

Made it to level 46 and they severely reduced the remote raids and are increasing the costs dramatically!!! They want us to walk the earth recording all the data we see, streets, landmarks, buildings, etc so they can sell it to whomever and when we choose to play from home because of weather, health issues etc they think they can force us back out!!! No thanks!! Was fun for awhile!

I'm very frustrated with this slow nerfing of the players experience. The changes over the years are just making it more and more difficult for regular players to enjoy the game. I also find the menus to be laborious. Once you catch a Pokemon for example you have to click so many times to appraise and tag or transfer it. This process should be much more streamlined.

Been playing off and on since launch. By and large I think the changes they've made have been solid, but some are just too glaring to ignore anymore. Slow to release updates (new pokemon specifically), continued stripping back of well-loved features (remote raids, breakthrough research), and circling the drain with the same few ideas has really been killing the game. Can't say its worth playing like it use to be.

I love this game, been playing since it came to the UK. However certain things are really starting to annoy me, for example, pokemon with incredibly low CP are somehow able to break out of ultra balls many times! Also, when battling, there should be an option to decline the mystery pokemon that you win. I've just used 60 pokeballs trying to catch one, all of my berries, multiple ultra balls and all of my great balls and STILL I haven't caught it! And I cant battle again till I've got it!

Edit 07/11/2018: the individual pokemon pages keeps crashing and there's no way to return to the pokemon bag view without exiting the game completely. Whilst it crashes, the favourite and appraise options, etc still work. __________ The app has come a long way. Game play is now a lot better and there are way more features. This game actually encourages me to go outside and go on walks. I do wish that more of the original 151 Pokemons will appear as these are the ones I'm familiar with from my childhood. Edit: after the recent update I have found that Pokemons break free a lot more frequently. For instance I might have had several good shots capturing the pokemon everytime but one has literally broken free more than 5 times. This is frustrating as it's too time consuming for one pokemon and depletes the pokeballs supply very quickly.

Released a game that isn't close to completion or first advertised. Update so that all users can't use. Update: 6-27-2020, I enjoy it more than when it first came out but they seemed to have reduced the spawn rate to zero in the majority of areas. Some places in town have a normal rate while walking, while others one street over have absolutely none. I don't understand what you label as a spawnable place.

I love this game, and I've been playing it pretty consistently since it came out. I wish there was an easier way to get coins besides spending money I don't have. The cap on what you can make in gyms and the fact that you just throw supplies away is very limiting. It would be cool to be able to sell your items, or when you vullaby's been in a gym for nearly a month without you being able to remove it it would be cool to get more than 50 coins. Seems kind of unreasonable.

Enjoyable if you're out and about a lot. Game sometimes hangs when you click on a wild pokemon- requiring you to restart the game and lose the pokemon you were just trying to catch. The AR scan task is quite irritating, particularly if you don't have access to get exactly where the marker is. Even when you can- I've stood on an AR gym many times and it still tells me to get closer to scan it, though there was physically no way for me to get on top of it more than I already was.

Started off rough, but got better. Gameplay is rather simple and gets boring. I do like the option to use the camera to use the real world as a background for catching Pokémon. It's nice for immersion. Not a fan of how trading was implemented. It actually discourages players from trading Pokémon that one or both people don't have by increasing the star dust cost to a ridiculous degree (that's right, you can't trade for free). Shiny Pokémon, or unique variations (such as the Santa hat Pikachu) also count as their own species, so you can't even trade shinies for a reasonable price unless you both already have it. It makes trading rather pointless.

I've just recently started playing this app again and it's better than it used to be but the distance measuring is off. I walked for three whole miles which is 4.82 km and it only gave me a .4 kilometer reading. So that still needs work. I still think this app is kind of pointless if you can't battle wild Pokemon like you used to in the games, or be able to battle other trainers outside of gyms. That would make the game much more realistic and more enjoyable so this app is average. But a good time killer nonetheless.

its a great game, but is virtually unplayable in most of my area of the US, outside big cities because it requires (relatively fast) mobile connection/internet, assuming there even is one. The infrastructure simply isnt there. The places I can play are far and few between, and the pokemon variety still isnt very great despite multiple updates. Gyms etc are very spread out and the most random places are marked as Pokestops. Will continue playing when ppl like us get a better experience.

I initially had a 5 star review for the game, it was buggy and unoptimized when it released, I've been playing since day one. While it has come a long way in performance, the monetization aspect is a deterrent. With the price of remote raids going up, it makes the game more restrictive. While the purpose of the game is "Go" the ability to remote raid reasonably made the game more accessible to those who cannot go out/other limitations. Very few new features/pkmn added to rationalize daily play.

This could be a great game and a wonderful expansion to the pokemon series. As it stand now, though, it is sub-par. At the release of the game it had an adequate tracking system, but with each update that tracking system gets worse until they now removed it altogether. They also lessened the radius that pokemon show up in the area and killed external tracking sites. Niantic, if you don't want players to use these sites, PROVIDE THE PLAYERS WITH AN ACTUAL TRACKING SYSTEM. Also, Niantic customer support sucks

Nothing good came from this new update. The game as a whole takes noticeably longer to load and has started to add strain to my battery. If this was for a good reason; I would understand, but it's not. It's a new map, and "lil' Debbie" character models that look just awkward in every way. I'm considering wasting coins on a mask to avoid my character models chunky little face in the corner. The pokemon models are starting to look just as awkward in both of their new backgrounds to boot.

Ok, so it has been a few years since my last review and I'll admit the game has got slightly better, the soundtrack is now set to loop and there are far more encounters to help collect candies to level up, thumbs up on that. However wild pokemon battles are still non existent and it is for this reason I can only give 2 stars. Come on Niantic fix this already.

The game is fairly entertaining. I do have a few complaints though. #1, you can't heal certain pokemon with the potions, even if all their power is out. #2, sometimes, you'll work on the tasks for special research. All is well until you realize the research says you didn't do it. (Ex. : Play w/ your buddy 10×, distracted by something shiny.) Now to the good stuff. The game helps people get out. The raids are fairly entertaining. The ability to play at home is also nice. Overall, pretty good game

"The pandemic is over so no more pandemic bonuses that made the game better!" "We have lootboxes but refuse to tell you the odds of what you'll get!" "We won't fix our bugs and will break existing features because why not!" "Grind for this temporary feature!" Niantic is suffocating their game and I'm glad I'm playing much less and watching from the sidelines.

I really love this game. But because I live in a town/not a city, there are so few gyms and pokestops in the area. Specifically where I live you cannot even see a gym on the screen, and there are 3 pokestops on the edges. I have to travel quite a few kilometers to find one. Been playing incredibly hard though and finally on level 35. But I'm growing tired of the limited experience from home since I can't do remote raids like other people can from their homes.

Nice if you move a lot without driving, the game mechanics are lackluster and requires large groups of people to capture tough Pokemon challenges. Good enough. (I also live in an area that Pokemon don't spawn so that might effect my review.) After some use the game will not load my location, I have tried several "fixes" nothing has worked nothing I can do in game anymore.

Game is good and so is the graphics. But the game keeps on freezing. I had to reinstall but it's the same issue. either scrolling through my inventory, pokemons or even doing raid battle and capturing, the game freezes for no reason. Cache is too many from this game i have to delete it everytime. Next time make the app 1gb plus so that all game resources are already in and no need to load. Please niantic read my review. I'm not the only one experiencing this problem.

Normally my go to! I haven't been able to get the game to open for a few days now. I uninstalled and reinstalled it and still nothing. Other than that I love the game. It's always a fun thing to check while walking the dogs or in between stops in town. I love the Gameboy versions alot more tho! I wish that battling your pokemon would help level them up not just poke candy. The walking is really inaccurate as well but other than that great fun

For the past week, I have been receiving "Failed to Login" error message when booting up the game. It has worked perfectly for the few years I've played this game, but this error is a first for me. I followed the many instructions online to fix the error, but none of them worked. So far, there's no word about the servers on official Twitter.

I played this game from launch until about two years ago, when I took a hiatus from it. After redownloading the game, I am appalled and horrified by the changes forced on players by Niantic. Adventure sync on Android used to be integrated in a way where it would only gather info on how far you walked. Now it needs to read your location all the time. That's way too much info. Need I even mention the remote raid changes? Pure corporate greed and sad to see a game I enjoyed so much fall so far.

The game when it initially came out, though a lot of server issues, was great. Super addictive and a childhood dream. However, with each update, the game continues to get worse and worse. Don't bother installing. You can't hardly do anything anymore anyway with the increased rates of Pokemon running away and the increased difficulty in catching pokemon. Everything they do, they do wrong.

I liked the idea, just the constant adds, changes, and going back on the pandemic things makes me not want to go out and explore the world anymore. Too little reward for grinding, they basically want you to pay, when in the original games at least medicine and healing was free. Took it off my phone, probably won't be back, not sure yet. Let's see how bad Niantic screws up more

I rated it one star when it came out, it was buggy and the company refused to answer questions or give information and much of the information that had come out was wrong and they had over hyped the game in relation to what they put out. Now, like 2 years later or more, the game is much better. I don't know if the company has gotten better at customer service, but the game is fun and worth playing. The prices for buying things in game are insane, you should never buy anything, but only playing it free is fine and it encourages you to go out and walk!

Fun game that encourages me to go out and walk! There are a lot of folks talking about bugs here, but I haven't been having problems. My main gripe is spoofers ruining the fun for people who want to play the game as intended. Some moderation so far as this is concerned would be really great. I know spoofers converge online to cooperate. There has to be a way to crack down on that. It really does make it frustrating sometimes. I'll be playing for as long as it's available!

I played this game for hours EVERY day for about one year since the games release date, Then rarely played it on and off ever since. I have gotten practically nowhere despite all this time and gym battles are still too intimidating. But the amount of grinding needed for gym battles is too demanding for most people, while a small handful of people dominate. Im not saying thats a bad thing, but be warned that this game demands a LOT of time. It took what seemed forever, but its a LOT better than it used to be. Only thing its missing is PVP. I love catching and managing my pokemon, I wish I could battle.

Other than all the complients about the 3 step being taking off (with or without it, doesnt make a difference if it doesnt work) the radar is sometimes inaccurate. But the biggest problem is how much more difficult it is to catch even a low level pokemon. Wasted many pokeballs cause pokemon spam attacks and jump way too much, and often run away (even with razzberries and great or ultra balls). Very frustrating having to waste so much. Hope Niantic fixes alot of things in the next update.

It makes no sense that pokemon spawn way more often in large cities than in rural areas. Also there are very few pokestops in rural areas so it is much more difficult for people who do not live in large cities. Also when you defeat a gym someone else who did nothing to help defeat it can just take it for themselves. The game is also still a bit buggy. If these issues get fixed I will update my review. Update: it got better. Not great, but better

I abandoned the game like many did 2 months into its initial release but came back during the anniversary event in 2018. Surprisingly the game is now at an enjoyable level with actual stuff to do, raiding with groups, trading with friends, and/or battling strangers. I gave this game a 2 star review at launch because it was an incomplete grind. Now though in 2019 it's a pretty good ARG. Go trade, battle, and explore. Whole communities have formed to make raiding and playing easier, just search.

The gameplay is super shallow considering how cluttered and labyrinthine the UI is. And yet still it always seems like the information you need isn't made available when you need it. For example, let's say you want to trade some Pokemon with me. This costs a currency called stardust. How much do you have? You gotta cancel the trade to go check. How much do you need? Unknown and, depending on how much you have, potentially unknowable. It's a mess.

Update 3.9.24 Game won't load. The phone says there's a bug. Update 4.5.19 - the upper limit of trainer levels needs to change. many of my friends are at 39 or 40 and not really interested in continuing. because of the limit. Also, there is still a glitch in catching lower level Pokemon, but it's improved. What I would like to see is virtual sharing, battling, or trading without having to be practically sitting in the other persons lap.

I have a lot of problems with getting randomly kicked out after hours or days of solid gameplay and all of the sudden an error message that tells me my login cant be authenticated. Sometimes resetting my password fixes the problem and sometimes it doesnt. And sometimes I'm left unable to log in for weeks. Hopefully this new update will fix these problems I've been having for a while now but if it will ever download I will see and update review.

The games servers are lacking. As usual Nintendo has under estimated the amount of people that are going to try to play. Also GPS location doesnt work very well. Half the time it says my GPS isn't working when it is. Samsung Galaxy S6 Btw. My biggest complaint is that it gets boring. You can't fight wild Pokémon (which is the entire premise of previous games and the show) and I think that is ridiculous. Step it up Nintendo.

Would be nice to be able to play the game without restrictions. I am able to walk, spin pokestops, and catch pokemon with no issues; but once it comes to opening a gym or even trying to pull up my profile, the game lags and kicks me back to my devices home screen. I've tried force stopping, uninstalling and reinstalling, and even went as far as doing a factory reset. Didn't have issues until the new update.

Here are my issues. 1. The battle system is awful you have to click to use one attack that you don't get to choose. 2.The leveling system is terrible because there are no real levels it's all based off of Combat Points (CP). 3. Catching Pokemon is just as bad you don't have to weaken them to catch them there is no challenge and it defeats the point of having a starter Pokemon in the first place.

I have had this game since day 1 and it has gone through some demo, but overall I am very happy with how the game turned out. Having originally thought it crashed way too much, I only gave a 2 star rating. Thank you for this game niantic team. The only thing i have to deduct 2 stars for is the fact that in small towns its impossible to beat 5 star raids. No other players and even if they were it would take too long to get to it, and due to that you wont capture certain pokemon.

Everything is a grind, many people use GPS spoofing and the handful of fun activities that exist have few rewards, all of which are entirely luck based. Unless of course, you want to spend cash. The game is dead. In its final stages its doing everything it can to take advantage of the handful of players left. If you're thinking about trying it again, don't bother. Everyone is years ahead of you anyway.

The game is fun to play, when it works. Every time I've played this game it's bugged out in some way, whether it's the pokeball not shaking when trying to catch a pokemon, or when a pokemon escapes from the ball but it doesn't zoom back out for me try throwing another one, both meaning I have to restart the app. Then usually after that it says I'm unable to log in. And that farce continues for a good couple of hours sometimes until I can eventually log back in again. Basically, it needs a load of patches...

For a major game it is very unreliable. Starting the game often freezes, sometimes it recovers, other times you have to kill and retry. Several times a day it will hang, especially if you are busy, and even more so when coverage is less than perfect. It seems like they have a very poor retry scheme and no hardening against network issues. Game play has been declining as the company tries to force people to play their way instead of encouraging people to engage.

Game is awesome, it let's me live my childhood dream of finding Pokémon in "real life" and I thank you for that 👍. Everything is great except that there is one thing that is bugging me and that is that the roads do not show up on my map. The Pokémon, gyms, and Pokestops do but the roads in my area don't. So it basically looks like I'm playing in a big field of grass haha. Please fix, just a small issue but it's bugging me. Thanks!!! EDIT: Thanks for the fix, game and updates are awesome.

So much potential wasted. Niantic was responsible for the first thing humanity came to world peace, yet they failed. I've played the game since it's launch and even though it was always littered with bugs, but it was okay because it was fun. They managed to improve the game even more during the pandemic, making the game more accessible to the less able. After that it all went downhill. They slowly removed or limited every good new feature. Last straw was doubling the prices in the in game shop.

It was enjoyable enough when I first started playing with my wife, but just like the pokemon company itself, the game has become stale, and I see very little interest in jumping back into it. The avatar changes were bad, but that's only one of many other problems with the game now. From the overpriced shop to the constant lag issues.

The game has less features than when it started out, and we can't even track Pokémon the way we're supposed to. Not even a little bit like the trailer. External sites are being shut down so instead of being a game to go out and play, it's a game I play when I go out. Back to regular inside gaming for me. After the update they made even more of a push for in app purchases by decreasing the catch rate. Gg way to kill a game.

Not enough of anything in rural areas. I live 15+ miles from the nearest town, it's not fair that cities have the easiest time playing the game. Please do something about this. (I wrote this original review in 2016. Sad it's 2021 and still the same for rural areas.... Redownload in hopes it was fixed for us to enjoy the game too. But I see you still don't care about us. Good job.)

When I first started playing this game, I strove to collect all of the Pokemon. However, now that so many Pokemon are region-locked or otherwise gated -- mostly in limited-time egg events with incredibly low odds that Niantic refuses to disclose -- I've given up on ever completing that goal. Strange Eggs are an egregious new addition, requiring a disproportionate amount of work for a high chance of hatching literal garbage. Megas, similarly, require a great deal of time and effort to essentially rent a powerful Pokemon for a few hours. Events are too frequent, but normal spawns between events are horrible because almost all of the desirable Pokemon are unavailable in the wild. I'm giving the app two stars because I still find that attempting to get gold gyms gives me an incentive to walk more, but I do not care about anything else in the game. I dropped from frequently buying coins to completely free-to-play a year ago, and I can't see that changing.

As of now in late 2019, the game has content. Tons of it. But the amount of cash grabs and poor decisions Niantic has made in the past few months alone warrants a lower rating. The base game is great, and a good way to go out and meet people and do things. But locking content behind paywalls and making raids unbeatable with less than 10 people seems like a step in the wrong direction. If you pick it up now DO NOT give Niantic any of your money, speak with your wallets ladies and gentlemen.

While the game is still glitchy and somewhat confusing, I must say that im loving the hell outta it! The idea of getting ppl outta their houses to catch pokemon is a nice spin on the typical poke' game. Now it's only getting 4 stars outta me because of said glitches (not to mention server crashes DX) and lack of a way to directly challenge your friends. Add in a friend's list and "meet up n' challenge" mechanic and that will more than make up for the glitches in my opinion. Other than that, Damn fine game!

I played this game for years now and im starting to enjoy it less ans less, simply because, with the recent update, Niantic are refusing to take into consideration players that either cant attend in person rais due to personal difficulties, or simply not having a large enough local community to deal with harder content, such as legendary and mega raids. However if this huge part of the game is to be overlooked, its still a pretty good game, but still, not as inclusive as it was and should be.

The new character update is trash. The "battle" system is atrocious with its latency and just isn't fun to begin with. If you're just looking to get Pokemon to transfer into mainline games, it's good for that. Beyond that it's just an insane money grab. You can't even get rid of eggs without hatching them with paid items, and with the recent pools there hasn't really been anything worth the effort or cost to hatch. Stop trying to push the newest starters. Nobody likes them.

I used to really really love this app and game, it was a fun way to get outside and experience Pokemon in a new way with friends. Lately though I started playing again and it's become more of a money grab than anything else. Coins to purchase items and items themselves in the shop are seriously overpriced. You're limited in what you can do without going through a paywall. Raids (only one free daily), appearance items, lures, etc. are premium items now you have to pay for with real money.

No help or tutorial at the start was dumb. And finding Pokémon takes forever, Thanks to the fact I don't live in a city. Great idea on straight up abandoning the countryside. Plus getting pokeballs is dumb, I get one or two from a stop. Should be given way more than that to be considered long term playable without paying which is clearly its main focus... I jump in and out but it's mostly just garbage and something to do for no real reason.

The game itself is great fun. Very well thought and gets more and more features. Regular events and a very nice community around it. The implementation on the other hand is poor at best. The game is full of bugs, kicking you out of raid battles for no good reason, errors out in the middle of anything. They obviously make a lot of money on the in-game purchases, I don't really get how they can low-ball their infrastructure.

I bought a few dollar worth of items, which is usually fine, however, if the servers aren't crashing, or the animation when you capture a pokemon freezes the screen, it just becomes a huge waste of money. I've WASTED the items I bought because I keep having to force close the app and reopen it, just to have the capture animation freeze over and over. DO NOT PURCHASE ANYTHING FROM THEIR STORE UNTIL THEY FIX THE STABILITY ISSUES. Very displeased because I know I won't get a refund or reimbursement

I've been playing since it came out, I did take a break from it for almost a year because I was having issues acquiring pokeballs. They have since fixed this.. Some of the more recent updates have been great but have issues, the battling freezes or lags causing some frustration. The remote raiding has been great. I do wish you had more time to join after getting an invite, i have missed out on some raids due to this. Also had it freeze battling raid bosses and missed out on the shadow pokemon

Don't get me wrong, I absolutely adore this game and it gives me a good reason to go outside, but it's hard to find Pokémon when the footprint feature doesn't work. The footprints are supposed to increase and decrease depending on how far or close you are to a Pokemon. It works fine on iPhone but not for Andriod, I hope this feature is fixed soon. It's really the only thing wrong with the game, everything else is absolutely wonderful.

Updated from my previous review (from 2016: 4 -> 3 stars). The gameplay has got more fun, and the previous issues are resolved. However the game is becoming more pay-to-play than it used to be. You now have to buy some special researches (not using the in game currency), and it is harder than ever to earn in game currency. It takes 3 days of acquiring the maximum daily coins in order to afford a single incubator, which is virtually impossible as it requires other people to beat your gyms daily.

Came back to the game after almost 6 years. Lots of new features. Game feels rewarding. Gym system is much better and you can easily get your 50 coins everyday. Only reason not 5* is that its pretty pay to win. I would give it 5 if you could get 150 coins a day. Would balance out the prices of things a bit and allow you to keep up with the people who spend a lot of money on the game.

I think they rushed the system. It's fun. Gets you to move about instead of being indoors. Meet new people. And it makes you feel like a real trainer. However the system itself is very buggy. Especially coming and going from Wi-Fi connection. It does tend to freeze on occasion. And the majority of pokemon that can be found are in places that can lead to police being suspicious. So all in all. Not the best. Sure with some more fine tuning and so forth the game could be awesome. Just not yet there

Recently, the game has gotten worse. GBL is unplayable, as it keeps giving the Weak Connection message. Yet my opponent is able to attack me perfectly fine. Doesnt matter what wifi I'm connected to, it's still unplayable. I even have issues logging into my game. It doesnt let me go in the game connected to my wifi, I have to always turn off my wifi just so the game can load. This game needs to be fixed asap. I know others are having the same exact issues, so I hope niantic provides some update.

This game is fun, it encourages you to get out and walk and explore new places. If you have played a pokemon game you will have fun with this. It has problems, the tracking is still spotty, and it drains batteries like crazy. The research is nice, it gives you a reason to log in every day and chances at legendary pokemon, the raiding is fun if you can find a group. Give it a try.

Very fun game, been playing it since launch. I'm disappointed that the performance hasn't gotten any better. It still only runs at half of the maximum refresh rate of the device even if the device is powerful enough to handle the full refresh rate. Please add a toggle to enable a high performance mode so we can play 60 fps on a 60hz display. The Harry Potter AR game runs at full speed, why can't Pokemon Go?

The game has changed a lot since its debut in 2016. Some changes are welcome like the peer to peer battle. Although it should have been an option from the start, its finally here. The poke tracker is finally in working order and I like the way they done it as the pokemon are easier to find rather than wandering around aimlessly like before. More to come after I use more with recent updates.

Update: Increased prices, decreases item effectiveness, and no remote trades are why I've given up on this game and uninstalled at level 43. Niantic just wants $ Game requires far too much effort to enjoy anymore, with little payoff. Been playing since release and I'm only level 40. They put too much incentive into paying for items and bag upgrades. The amount of footwork that goes into getting to level 35 using Pokemon gyms to pay for bag upgrades to hold much needed items is actually insane.

01/29/21 Many times the game is harder just because you use s special item like pineapple or a berry. So you miss out on the extra candy and XP because of this. 06/24/22 - The servers STILL have problems. Whenever I have time to play the game, it cycles itself as if it's trying to load data but can't. So the game freezes or is stuck. The game has too many problems to even make it worth your time. Freezing in raids, getting kicked out of the game after a raid ends. Too many issues to list here.

I spend far too much time on this game. Following the most recent update, however, this is likely to change. The buddy section no longer loads, meaning that it will take longer to upgrade and will also deny "gifts" that it brings. It was bad enough that you decided that we couldn't play long distance raids, but this is ridiculous. Kinda defeats the object when you can't play the whole game. Thumbs down, Niantic.

Good but could be great. Niantic doesn't like to keep quality of life improvements. I've uninstalled the game after playing for years. Such a grind of a game that encourages you to pay money to make life easier. Some challenges can not be done unless you get lucky and raid with some big group or pay for remote passes and use pokegenie for matchmaking.

I've been a player since the beginning, and came back in 2020 after a hiatus. The game *was* great, and then Niantic started rolling back changes and improvements that they made during COVID in the name of "rebalancing" the game. All in the name of making more money, more like it. They no longer care about the player base, just their bottom line.

I have been having a lot of issues with this game and the only way to fix it is to have e to uninstall and reinstall everyday. it gets very annoying. I have lost a lot of money on pokeball glitches too. This game keeps getting worse. Now no stops or gyms will show up and its been like that for days. Id give this zero stars if I could. It is no longer playable on any level. Also can someone make it so I dnt have to be logged in to talk to support cuz half the time it wnt let me log in.

Overall I enjoy the app; however, what I don't understand is how a game that's been out this long and is backed by a massive company like Nintendo has such garbage servers. This is the only app I can't play online on my wifi, I constantly get disconnected from online battles for no reason. So apparently this game is more network intensive than most modern shooters, as I can play those over my wifi with no issues. It's very frustrating and I hope it will be fixed soon.

Just disappointed with the game that could have been the best like no other ever was. Played at launch 2016 but left the game after 2 months due to servers and limited features. Returned July 2023 thanks to friends and was impressed that it took 6 years to finally implement the basic pokemon features. I was most impressed with remote raids, but of course that's now unusable due to price increase and limited. One thing that hasn't changed, Niantic doesn't care about players nor about the game!

I love Pokemon and have played GO since its debut. However, Niantic's poor decisions and refusal to address what players want has reached a new low. The increased Pokestop/gym interaction distance (and other pandemic bonuses) should be permanent, as they make the game safer and more accessible for EVERYONE regardless of the pandemic. The pandemic is far from over and acting like it isn't is irresponsible at best. This combined with the constant bugs is the last straw. I will not be purchasing anything else in-game, at least until I see Niantic listening and communicating with its playerbase.

Very fun and addicting game. However, the two setback I have is that you can only get 50 pokecoins a day (LIKE WHY?!?! There is literally no point for that to exist in this game), and the new models for your trainer. Even though there were only two models (male and female), they still look more lifelike then these abominations. I can't even combine certain accessories anymore. Maybe it's just nostalgia for playing the game for so long, but PLEASE at least make the old avatars an option.

2016 Very addictive. I can't log in half the time but when I can I can't fault the game. My dogs never been walked so much. New review. 2022 still playing on and off. My son is into it now. Sadly though I can't seem to upload pokestop scans, it just crashes and the adventure sync doesn't work for either of us. Other then that. Brilliant game. X

Loads of fun, the new trainer battles allow for tons of fun and competitive play. The consistent updates add new content all the time, to keep the game interesting. If I had to pick something to improve on, I would say to make the pokedex feel more like a pokedex. Give us information about pokemon we have bumped into, or caught. Knowing generally what areas to find pokemon gives people a reason to explore.

I gave it three stars because I like playing the game but very frequently I find myself "unable to authenticate" after most major updates and as a result, I can't play the log in to play the game. I had used the in-game purchase store to use a lucky egg, switched apps, switched back to Pokemon go, and was unable to log back in; essentially wasting actual money. I know other people who are unable to log in and I think after all this time that the game has been out with all of the major players, they'd be able to fix this issue/avoid it but it's still an issue I can expect after every update. Anyone have work arounds to this issue?

Fun, especially if you walk a lot. Rating their bug support. Had all field research disappear overnight. Not a major issue, but I wanted them to know especially with research-based events coming soon. I didn't expect to get anything more than an automated response, but they replied saying that was impossible and that maybe someone else did it. I don't share my account, have no children, and am familiar with the game and how the research should stay indefinitely. Too condescending for bug support

Look guys, it is a great game, still a great thing on off time but we severely need things. First off the storage is a severe problem, we don't wanna pay, ok? Second, You severely need to do so connectivity and anti lag updates. I have full belief that you can fix the game and make it great again but you gotta try. I'll put a 5 star if you could get these out.

It is impossible to play this game fully without paying exorbitant amounts. I downloaded the game when it first came out and deleted it when I realized this. Was told by friends that it's gotten better so I downloaded it again 2 years later. This time I spent $10 to see how long 200 pokeballs will last.... I'm on day 4 and I'm down to 40. The escape rate of pokemon is ridiculous and only set that high to get people continuously spending money. Like I said, I've tried this game twice.... I won't be trying a 3rd time.

I'm experiencing the same login problems as everyone else since the latest update. My husband is in the same boat. We both play on Android phones. We are hoping a new update will correct the problems soon... I'll come back and give the game a much better review if I'm ever able to play again... Edited: since fixing the problems above the app had been working well, just occasional issues.

There are too many main research quests that are long term goals. I get that they encourage people to play for prolonged periods, but some of em depend on the pokemon that appear in the area, which is totally out of my control and frustrating. And of course, as it always has been, high rank raid battles are hopeless for solo players especially in quarantine. Lately it keeps telling me to update the app but there's nothing to update??? What is going on?

Playing was fun at the start because of the steps-tracker. But not being able to TRACK a mon is beyond frustrating!! EDIT: New tracking system is worse! Showing ONLY Pokestops encourages driving if they are too far away, instead of walking to NEARBY pokemon. Can only track if near a Pokestop. Been playing since the beginning and am a dedicated player. If I didn't have a spawn spot in my house or work, I wouldn't play at all now. Please, BRING BACK TRACKING!!!

Niantic had implemented fantastic changes that made the game interesting and fun for players in rural areas or in situations that make travel/walking difficult. They have decided to turn their backs on all those players by prioritizing in-person raids and geolocation data. I am disappointed by these changes that make the wonderful Pokemon universe less accessible for a wide range of players (non-city folks). I will reinstall the game if Niantic shows consideration for its player base.

After 4+ years of playing this game, it has become apparent that Niantic cares more for money than ease of access for players, the paywall created recently has hindered game play and continues to do so. There are ways around the gross money grabs, but you will never experience the full game without dishing out AT LEAST $40/year in events and bonus items. I will give 4* due to the fact that playing enough will circumvent the need to pay money (outside of events), but expect a grind to make it up.

When I was 10 years old (20 years ago), all I wanted was to catch Pokemon in the world. While the premise of this game is exciting, it's pretty clear now the game was not ready for release. It's nearly unplayable at this point and gets pretty boring in the higher levels. My biggest issue though is the fact that there are no trainer vs. trainer battles. I'm leaving Pokemon Go alone until it's actually done and picking my 3DS back up.

Pokemon Go has come along way since its beginning. It runs smoother, has more to do and the events are great. There is still alot of activity even in the smaller suburbs or towns and the seasonal roster and event roster pokemon are a great edition. My only complaint is that the character is the same for everyone. There are so many types of characters in the game from pokefans, scientists, bug catchers and fisherman. They should be entered as an avatar for players.

I really enjoy the game most of the time but there are a few big problems. The updates are huge, 90% of the time they don't work, I have to close everything out and restart my phone multiple times. The feedback system is tedious + doesn't work. Too many of the challenges are based on routes or playing with other people now. And it's complete bs that you only get 50 coins no matter how long a pokemon is in a gym. If you have multiples in gyms, it doesn't even count as you can only earn from one

It's a fun game to play to kill time, I just wish it didn't take SO LONG to level up. Also sometimes when the circle is green and I'm using my BEST poké-balls to catch a Pokémon WHILE using berries, they escape. Or when they pop up on my screen, I'll click on them to try and catch them they just disappear. It's really is a great game and gets me out of my comfort zone, but there are a few inconveniences within the game. I can handle them but its just bothersome.

Great game but a few things bother me. 1. Cant get rid of Premium Raid passes and I have 22 eating up storage. 2. When first opening the app pokemon will appear almost immediately then disappear and take about 30 seconds to a minute to reappear. 3. When it comes to pokestops a lot of the times I get "try again later" more often then I should. Gets really annoying. Otherwise the game is great and I play it every day almost religiously. Please let me get rid of the raid passes. Also would be great if we could sell the extra items instead of trashing them. Maybe for some random candy or for pokecoins.

Update to my update: years later, I'm still playing and having as much fun as ever, and would have even more fun if it with too less time to appraise and access Pokemon to keep for whatever reason and what to transfer OR if they arrived our storage issues, possibly by giving us a home base type mass storage dump. With so many different aspects to the game and so many Pokemon to collect, many of us would play the game way more (and thus, spend more money on it) if we had a mass storage solution.

My review has changed, they made pokemon more frequent, and pokestops are no longer an issue, they've popped up everywhere. A lot of the warts this game had at launch, have been alleviated by a development team that listened to their userbase, and has given them what they want. It took some time, but they delivered in spades. Niantic is a good example of what video game publishers should be doing.

I love Pokémon. Played since '98. This game started off so strong and continues to ruin itself with every update. There have been a lot of updates to help with the Covid-19 situation we're all in, but overall, I still am not impressed by any means. I'm always more disappointed with "fixes and adjustments"; With the latest update, the game lags so much that it's costing me resources. I'm upset the Pokémon Company trusts their franchise with Niantic, but I do hope they don't repeat the mistake.

Its great so and they've added a few of the things i wanted them to add, but i still have a few more things if like to see. That said, the fact that they added to and improved the game earned them star #5 1)The ability to locate fellow trainwrs as long as both trainers are on each others friends lists. 2)trading of items and candies. 3)the ability to train/level our Pokemon through battling, and maybe even being able to engage wild Pokemon.

I absolutely love this game. As an ongoing pokemon fan this is the closest thing to catching them irl. However, since the recent 0.33.0 update, I have not been able to see gyms, not pokestops. I also get nothing in the nearby listing, even in highly populated areas I have been going to practically scince I started the game. I would love to continue playing, but if there is nothing for me to interact with in the game, I have nothing to enjoy. I hope the programmers get the bugs under wraps soon.

While I didn't personally love this game, it was a great way to get people exercising. Most of my extended family love it. When this first came out, I felt it was SEVERELY pay to win. I now know this is not true. Paying gives you slight advantages, basically getting things early, such as lures. In the later game, you DO get most items from spinning pokestops. 4 stars because special trades costs. I can't afford 1 mil for a shiny eevee. Last thing, didn't personally like controls, but were usable

I've been playing this game since day one and I've been blown away with how many features they keep adding. If you played this game early on but stopped due to lack of content, I highly recommend you give it another shot. Gyms have been overhauled, there's research tasks, raids, team rocket, pvp, trading, and so much more in the works. Quite ironically sometimes I feel a bit overwhelmed with how much there is to do now. It's a great game and it motivates you to be active even in the winter.
daily eggs randomly get stuck at 1km then disappear sometimes. simultaneously using a lure and an incense only attracts a few pokemon

i love this app, but I wish it was better designed for small communities as well as cities. My nearest gym is nearly a mile away, in a low-traffic part of town. Since the time they were introduced, I've only ever participated in one raid because either I can't get to the gym in time, or I can get to the gym but no one else is there. It's frustrating that so many things rely on raids and the assumption that everyone around you is also playing.

I enjoy the game pretty well. Though it can be laggy, unresponsive, the throws will curve to the side a LOT when throwing straight, and the GPS needs to be refined a little more. Also, I would love it if there was a nudge option added for if a friend has an unopened gifts from you. I have some friends that are online daily but they don't send gifts. But I know it's because they forget. Maybe have a notification of a gift not being opened after 24 hours

This app has improved so much in the last two years. There's a lot more to keep someone interested in the game and playing. Most of the time the features work flawlessly but occasionally you get a hiccup, for example, using a camera and then going back to game causes it to reboot even with the Pokemon Go Plus Bluetooth device. I'd still like to see a Poke center where you can heal up Pokemon, buy specific moves from a TM/HM seller (legacy moves available on specific days) maybe put an Easter egg in the Poke center as an arcade game version of Red/Blue, and maybe a wonder trade station too. I'd also like to see some Team Rocket missions where you defeat them to unlock some difficult items to find or a special pokemon but these missions require a team building aspect like Raids do. Instead of bonuses for one team working together, bonuses for working across team lines to establish a Good vs. Evil type of dynamic. It would also be pretty cool to see the train at a gym to build it come back but more like a bonus to a pokemons stats when placed in a gym. Maybe training at a gym could slow the rate of decay all Pokemon in that gym experince, or maybe a 1% boost in max CP for two hours with a maximum of 5%

I love the intention behind the game, and its pretty easy to play while still allowing the player to find activities within that are more advanced. The problem I have is the seeming randomness of catching Pokemon, and I don't really think the environment plays a factor in what spawns. I notice the same Pokemon no matter if I'm near water or in a park.

There is so much in this game now. But no kids play. Or at least not many. Mostly people in cars driving around taking gyms. Some days it's a pain but others not so much. I used to go for walks hours at a time with this game. But I had my fun. I just turn it on from time to time to set what's going on. Edit 2023 sep. Coin cost went up. The game is doing too many different events. Players are aggressive with gyms in my area. I think I need to move on. Most task require no walking. I want to walk.

If you just want to catch Pokemon on a leisurely stroll or on the bus, you may have fun. However the game has become problematic. Legendary raids are difficult without 5+ people, and newly introduced mechanics made it difficult to join remotely. It has become nearly impossible for rural players and busy adults to have a full gameplay experience. I've been playing since 2018 and have sadly set it down till the company becomes much more player friendly.

VERY DISAPPOINTING. Pokemon Go used to be fun, engaging, and a daily play for me. Recently, Niantic (the parent company) has made COTINUED changes to this game that have made the game unplayable. From the constant bugs, to removing key features, and or pricing remote raid passes sky high, they have killed an amazing game, and experience. It's such a shame. Don't waste your time with this game, it's nothing more than a data collecting, money grubbing, bug filled mess.

This game has gone downhill. Fast. It's a money grab. The company doesn't listen to the fan base, and the game it's self is OK at best. Not to mention, even if you find rare pokemon, They're gonna just run away or be locked behind a pay to play wall. Honesty, if you want a better time catching pokemon, get Scarlet/Violet, or Sword/Shield. For the time and money it takes to play GO, it's easier to buy mainstream.

Still enjoy this game. The community day events are a fun motivator to get out and socialize, and brought us together with friends we hadn't seen in a long time. Raids are less of a temptation now and more of an "if we happen to be there" part of the game. We got burnt out on them because so many legendaries were run back to back to back in such a short amount of time. GPS issues still plague the app and can make certain timed events exceedingly frustrating, but over all I still enjoy the game most of the time.

Pretty fun game. However, you need to live in the center of big cities to get the most out of it. I can understand pokéstops being as they are now, but the logical thing would be having pokemon outside, in the actual wilderness... Can't play solo anymore, Gyms and raids require you team up with others, but when there is no one on your level around (everyone is at high levels nowadays it seems)...

A few suggestions that would bring up my rating. 1. Add the ability to put lures on gym poke-stops. We can spin them, they give us poke-stop goods; some places literally only have gyms so it needs to happen. 2. Add a way to call back a Pokemon who's been at a gym for a long period of time. It's obnoxious when they've already gotten their coins and they're being fed still, essentially stuck forever. 3. Finally, a sticker collection book please because they're just super adorable.

In the beginning, there were lots of glitches: had to restart the game in order to unfreeze the app constantly, so I was happy to update in the hopes things would be better. Bad news is, now all Pokestops & gyms have disappeared. I know it's not the GPS since I can still catch Pokemon & see where I'm at & it's accurate as I move around.  Tried logging out & back in; even restarted my phone. The problem remains. I've got few poke balls left. Here's hoping for another update soon so I can play on. :(

Great game just started playing again after taking a break for a couple years. The one thing I'm finding that hasn't changed and is one of the reasons I stopped is how much pay to play this game is. Every resource such as incubators raid passes and so on has to be purchased. Which wouldn't be a problem if you could either earn more coins from gyms each day or they at least lowered the cost of these items so you don't have to wait 4 plus days to buy and incubator that's going to last you a day.

It's an OK app. I mostly just like collecting and evolving the different types and styles of pokemon there are. However, in order to do that in a somewhat timely manner you gotta participate in the battles, raids, research, etc. Which I don't mind doing but the amount of players joining the battle leagues with back to back to back charged attacks straight out the ball is baffling. The fact that there is so many unchecked cheaters on the app really concerns me for the rest of my data privacy.

I do like this game however I think that getting an item like metal coat, sunstone, etc are very hard to get. Also getting legendaries Is extremely hard and I feel like that should be fixed because half the time you can catch them, the other half you cant. Another problem is that it is very hard to get pokecoins, like sometimes I would put my pokemon in a gym and then it takes forever for it to go out.

There are a ton of problems. First of all the servers are awful but we know that already. Second the gym battles never work and when they do you may not even get the gym. You can have spent 10  minutes battling your way through three trainers and some nobody from another team can take the gym while you are getting your victory text in game. Then you have to repeat the process or give up. Should really add a feature where you have to participate in gym battles to take the gym. Overall very disappointing.

I am really enjoying the game and would love to give it a good rating, but I am constantly getting issues, crashing, freezing up and graphical issues too.
