These are all things that I can work around as they don't stop my progress. But the main issue I have, is Pokémon in gyms, they will be in there for 12 or more hours, get knocked then get knocked out. I'll get the notification to get pokecoins, but when I look, I haven't received any, this has happened a lot of times it's stopping me raiding.

It used to be a great game. The changes they are making are not worth continuing to play. This is not a free to play game. You had something golden, and you've decided to put greed ahead of user experience, content, retaining players. Sad, I spent thousands of dollars over the years but I'm hanging up my trainer title. I'm a level 50 trainer from day one and I'm sad that niantic has really continued to sink a great game.

I've been playing this game since day 1 and I have never before seen a game company so fit to be dunked on as this. Niantic have shown time and time again that they simply only care about getting money and gathering your data. Recent changes to their raid system and shop have made it impossible for many of the long term players to actively enjoy the game without spending ludicrous amounts of money. Do not download the game until these issues are addressed by Niantic (which they never will be)

There are many issues that compromise the fundamental enjoyment of the game. There needs to be some sort of tracking. It doesn't have to be a specific location but at least bring something in that allows you to know if you're getting close or too far away. Lack of variety of pokemon spawning in rural areas is an issue. The gym update means anyone can take a gym. The new buddy system is an attempt to stop you hoarding useful berries and getting rare candies more easily.

A fun and entertaining game. Plenty has been said of its non-sedentary benefits. But it's a memory hog! Cannot have almost any other apps in memory at the same time. For this latest update on my old Galaxy S5, I have to play storage management shuffle yet again. It's not worth the trouble. Well, maybe when the game update links your Pokemon to their Pokedex entries; I might have a new phone by then.

Great game, absolutely love it. I will warn you though unless you want the event specific pokemon, go fest tickets are a complete waste of money because the game rarely ever works during them. Constant connection lost, pokemon appear and disappear instantly. You'd think after this many years it would have been fixed but it's like Niantic doesn't even try.

There are still some frustrating stuff , that seem easy to fix and provide a better experience. Pokemon in gyms that are not challenged can stay there for months. There should be a way to claim them back. Less trade challenges please. Some of us don't have a lot of friends, who play the game, around. Also, pvp is pretty boring. Other than that, fun game.

Great idea, needs to work on the execution. If you live in the suburbs or rural areas, this game will be a bit of a pain to play. Same entry level pokemon for a good while. Often laggy and freezes your phone, is a battery drain. But when working, is a lot of fun. Just be prepared to travel a lot if you don't live in a big city or you will only see pidgeys and rattatas for miles

*update: Niantic is listening and giving us what we want, time to come play!* I've been playing this game almost since inception. I've seen many players come and go. We're all starving for a legendary. The game has been lagging a lot lately, at gyms, at Pokéstops, during evolutions. The walking system isn't great with distance. I actually kept the game going during an official 5k walk, it only counted 3.2 on newly incubated eggs. I checked the route when I got home, it truly did cut that much off. No reason egg hatching takes so long. I have a new phone less than five months too! And NOW, I can't even play Pandora while playing the game, it force shuts. THAT'S UNCALLED FOR, FIX IT!

This app has come a long way from where it started, but is still the same core game that I started to enjoy in the beginning. The development team clearly had shown their skill but pushing out frequent updates that include bug fixes, efficiency improvements, and adding even more Pokémon into the game. The Pokémon games have been most of my childhood and having them (legitimately) on a mobile platform is the best thing in the world. I wish i could give more than 5 stars

I played pretty heavily when the game first came out then took a long break after the Summer. I came back to the game and the larger radius made the game so much better. Now they've taken that away for, what I can imagine, more in-app purchases since people wouldn't be able to flip as many pokestops. It just sucks that a game that I really enjoyed would stoop to such a predatory measure, especially after their playerbase invested so much time and money into it. Please revert the radius value.

Bring back the discount for remote raid 3-pack. 100 for single and 250 for 3-pack. I miss playing. Any recommendations for something a little less money-grabby? Still have not fixed the pricing. Very uninclusive to those with special needs, or just without an abundance of time or local players. My raid group has fizzled out and many will probably never install again. So disappointing.

My original review was pretty harsh. But since 2016 the game has come a long way, is quite flushed out and has something for players of all types, even if you are in a smaller town. It's now gone from a 1* to a 4* game for me. If they revert back the PokeStop distance issue (search on YT for the controversy), I might even bump it to 5*.

Why is there a limit on how many gifts you can send/receive?! We already can't send more than one gift per day to each friend so why limit how many we can send overall or open? And please update the friends list to include the actual date the person was online last. Not just "today", "yesterday", and "2+ days ago". It's irritating to have to constantly keep track of which friends are active and which ones have abandoned the game and are just wasting space on your friends list.

The initial bugs were annoying but this game has great potential. I hope the devs. don't give up on this. UPDATE: This game has progressed phenomenally and I don't need to tell anybody how fun this game is. I will say that the total item amount you can hold is kinda small and maybe my pokemon storage could be bigger but I bought more space so I'll survive. I just wish you could catch all the pokemon without having to get more space to do so. That's what I'm doing at least.

Great game but there is a problem within it that's kind of laughable. If you were to buy PokeCoins with real money, its gets more expensive the more you buy, rather than cheaper for more as most games do. For example, 100 PokeCoins in .99c, yet 550 PokeCoins is roughly $7. The trend continues with higher values as well. As you can see, you get more value if you were to buy multiple at .99c. Really weird mechanic and so surprised it has not been changed yet.

This game has so many cute Pokémon and you get to design your character. Also you can evolve,catch,battle with Pokémon and do missons. Then you get to chose a pattern for your journey. But you have to buy a lot of stuff with real money 💰. If you lose wifi you are stuck in the middle of nowhere. It's been a month and still haven't changed at all. So get this game if you want but it's a waste 🗑 of money 💰!!!!!!

EDIT: I am still casually playing this game. There have been a lot of improvements over time. I appreciate that they still support older OS. The game is kind of fun with collecting the different types of Pokemon, but unless you live in a diverse geographic area, you might have difficulty finding them. I have played over a year and mostly find only about a dozen types.

It plays well and was fun when it first came out. It feels a bit overwhelming trying to play as of late, especially considering that a lot of it feels like busy work. When it comes to Niantic games you've got Ingress with its "go to the place and do the thing," Pikmin Bloom with its "set it and and walk around" which feels more active, and then PokemonGO which feels like "stop every few steps to do a thing but also go to these places and do the thing." I WANT to love this game, but I don't.

Previous review: Servers down, poor execution on launch, would've expected more from a nintendo licensed game. Edit: Years after my review that was highly critical for no reason, i have started playing pokemon go again. Tons of added features make this a great casual game for me to play on the go. I highly recommend this for the lovers of the pokemon series, as an alternative to pokemon sword and shield which had a bit of controversy around its initial launch.

Can you please make it so we can get steps from other apps and not just "Google fit"? It's such a bad app for tracking steps. And now that we've been in quarantine so many months it's been more obvious. For instance if I use my elliptical or rowing machine it doesn't register any steps, but I can't get out to actually "walk"! Please consider opening up to all fitness apps, the quarantine won't end soon, and besides one should be able to play and not get exposed to an illness anymore.

Update about a year later: nothing from my previous review has changed. The game was fun when it came out but now it is predatory. Everything rolled out during the pandemic has slowly been rolled back and then some. They raised the prices for remote raids so unless you can physically go to areas (driving won't work as there are speed limiters), you cannot "Catch 'Em All!" This game seems to have diminishing returns the more you play, and as a lifelong Pokémon fan it is truly disappointing.

I used to love this game. It's definitely gone downhill. The research is busted. Take a snapshot of X pokemon. Ok. I did. Does the game recognize this? No. This issue has been reported and has been going on for months with not fix in sight. Also, glitching graphics, see your trainer standing still then all of a sudden it's like a flash of smeared trainer before snapping back to normal. Step it up!

To be honest i didnt expect this. They added gyms and pokestops making it possible to have tons of pokeballs. When i quit the only thing you could do was to catch and to battle (in gyms) now you can trade, battle each other, send gifts to friends and more. An lastly but the most important change is that they added a variety of pokemon to my area making the game enjoyable. Overall the game became great for my area and i want to believe for other areas like mine.

The game is without a doubt nothing less than an eye opener to the outdoors. Ever since I installed this game, walking outside has never bothered me once. However, it is difficult to get anything from the PokeStops since they are so scattered. The nearest PokeStops is at least 10km from my home and I have little access to such locations, and walking 5km has started to become more and more difficult as summer began. Also, its impossible to address this to anyone in the Pokemon GO developers, wth.

Way to be ableist and greedy Niantic. I've been playing since the beginning and have been a fan, but you keep taking away quality of life improvements for no reason other than "It's supposed to be an excercise app." And you're greedy. Raid passes increasing and being limited is the most recent, but also incubators only working while walking was a huge draw back that made me play less. I can't play at work. I get at least 15,000 steps a day. Last thing I want is to excercise more to play a game.

It's a lot of fun game. I enjoy that I 've get out my room and search for new pokemons. The new feature, trainer battle is owesome. But, I've found its difficult to find other trainers nearby. It will be so much easier and helpfull if you add some feature like a radar to detect where is the other trainer around and also we (players) can challenge them without say hello to them (in real). It is weird sometimes that you have to make contact with strangers only to playing a game. Thank you.

The game itself is great. It's entertaining and gives even the laziest couch potato incentive to go outside and walk around. Or it used to. With the new tracker, you're shown exactly where the Pokémon is, and you're not shown any unless they are by a Pokestop, so you've lost the incentive to go look for a rare one that randomly spawned nearby. I'd rather see all the ones nearby (even without spexific location) than know what's by a spot that I'm going to visit anyway. And it burns your battery faster.

I couldn't even get onto the app. It would load, and then I'd try to make an account and it would take to long to load. I would leave my phone on for hours, and the app wouldn't load the screen where I could make an account with Google. I don't like the apps overall experience either. Groudons are extremely hard to catch, and you can't find any starter pokemon. The only other time I found so thing else was the eevees. This app is a waste of time, and a waste of space.

Takes up WAY too much space on my phone, and AR+ doesn't work, and normal AR mode was removed because they apparently only care about people who can afford to buy brand new phones. The game lately seems very slow, sometimes taking several minutes just to open the camera option, and making scrolling through my Pokemon very time consuming. I once timed it, and it took three solid minutes just to accept and send a gift to one single person.

The playing mechanics are great for a mobile game and the concept finally got me to excersise willingly. However like for most other players, the servers are down half the time (or more). Knowing the amount of hype this game had before release, the servers should've been prepared for something like this. Please fix this issue as I personally find it the only thing from seeing Pokemon GO as a 5-star app.

Functionally the game works. Purchases are still hit and miss. The rewards road doesn't work at all and support doesn't respond. Why have a web store when it only loads the home page and not the store.

Never been into pokemon but I've become obsessed with this game. So much fun, BUT not being able to fill your pokedex because of area specific pokemon, the lack of being able to find some more often like Charmander, and the lack of finding new ones after a while, kills people's urge to play. Also, only getting .10 after a whole day of being on a gym is crazy. The time should be shortened, or amount raised. Edit: gotten a lot better

I used to play this game all the time back when it launched. After a long while, they finally added new things to the game that were much needed. My main concerns are that updates take way too long to come out, lack of pokemon still, raids are a pain to do since no one participates anymore, gathering items is tedious (especially since you'll commonly get the same low level items and can only buy low level items.), grinding is a tease for pokemon like Altaria, etc. Pay attention to your game.

Fun if you're a fan of pokemon. Raid battles require groups of people and as the game ages, I find less people playing. The introduction of friends, trading and tasks have increased gameplay and has done wonders. We could use an in game chat for friends or maybe the introduction of groups...? Also once you have entered a gym, defending it is uneventful.

Pokemon Go could be a great app but the shear number of bugs that have not been addressed or fixed and the amount of times that the app crashes or freezes up is insane. Update, Pokemon Go has gotten nothing but worse. It has to be one of the worst apps. and Niantic couldn't care less. They issue bug fixes that just causes more problems. The app. now crashes constantly or simply freezes. Now my wife's phone and mine is no longer compatible. Not gonna buy a brand new phone to play a broken game.

I have recently hopped back on and I can definitely say that it is still the same as I remember, which is good, but I do hope that they implement something better than the remote raid pass. Maybe a spoofing feature that everyone can use, like an item or something. I know some players can't go out like they used to before, or still have concerns or guidelines to follow for COVID. Also, there are barely any players in my location who do raid battles so that sucks as well.

It's odd that my original review disappeared; here we go again. If you enjoy Pokémon, I don't need to explain this game to you. You know it exists. Niantic has had a strained relationship with their customers from bugs for paid events and recently reducing accessibility the range to a Pokémon that they had increased during the pandemic. The players were vocal and, for once, Niantic listened. They promised additional changes. Taking things away from people. 🤦‍♂️

I like this game with the bug fixes and additions, but the support team is very unwilling to actually address or add/remove pokestops and gyms when you report it. three years later, and we are still at three stops and one gym in our town and one stop in the middle of nowhere that cannot be reached safely, and nobody will just pick a different place to create a stop. kinda insane.

It was fun for a week when things were more stable. GPS is all over the place (Nexus 5 T-Mobile). Very grindy. I do like that it's not really pay to win. Even if you do put money into it you still have to get out and walk to hatch eggs, get any balls better than regular, potions, revives, actually find Pokémon , and fight Gyms. There are still allot of bugs. One of the most annoying is not being able to track Pokémon which is a huge part of what makes this game a game. You just have to get lucky.

Love this game but cant ever reliably log in to it. Would spend money on it but its so damn buggy and the authentication to log in is at about 10% for me. Very disappointing. Huge name, huge IP, little to no actual care to grow their players or their game. Unbelievable. Fix your game. This is a major money maker for you. All you have to do is let players log in and add some cool and exciting features that the players have been begging for. Currently this app is a disgrace to the name of Pokemon.

The game at its core is great. Catch Pokemon using your real world as a map. Unfortunately, the Pokemon IP is the only thing keeping this game afloat. This game is plagued by the decision making and tone deaf approach of the developers to take away many beneficial QoL changes for the sake of their "vision" that cannot and will never align with the player base. Add on to that, many bugs and issues that they refuse to address, I believe this game does not have a long term future anymore.

I've been playing since 2019. It used to be better, as many are saying. The current problem with mine is that even though adventure sync is turned on, it's not working. I only collect kms when the game is running (and eating through my battery, even though I'm not playing). My other complaint is that when they redid levels, they gave you tons of items (awesome), then later said, "Oops here's 200 extra storage." Yet, I'm still out of storage from the level change. 🙄

I love this game, and the only reason I'm giving it a bad review is because Niantic has refused to address its players concerns about the new changes to raiding. (Raids limit and almost double the cost in passes) I don't like companies that don't listen to their player base, but I've also put enough time in to at least still be a casual player. It is very fun, just know what you are getting into.

I used to love playing pokemon go and I still play it now, but more and more features exclude players in remote areas. Thinking about raiding (at least we have remote Raids now) and now the next one the routes. I am living on an island with a couple of gyms and about 20 pokestops, we finally were able to create routes ourselves but it's taking forever to get them approved, I feel like the game has turned into an app where the money making has priority over the actual enjoyment of the players.

I would rate lower if I could. The game is completely unplayable now. Crashes and bugs at every corner. I can't even click on a Pokemon to try and catch it without the game crashing - but yet every single other app on my phone works just fine. It's sad because this game used to be great. Used to be. The disconnect between Niantic and their players is a total drag. Get it together... I'm angry I've spent money in this game and I can't even play it anymore.

It used to be good but Niantic went full predatory mode. Their prices keeps coming up (from 100 to 195 tokens for remote raids. That's stupidly huge). They offer special loot boxes with better rewards but only if you don't have enough token so you're forced to buy if you want the deal. If you have a lot of tokens tho, you can't have that deal... They don't care about their player base. I don't recommend playing this game.

Love the game for someone like myself but upon thinking about it the mechanics of it make it incredibly uninclusive , I know that's cryptic but unfortunately the character limit means I can't go into full detail about the issue, I even had helpful suggestions on how you could fix the issue and still have the game be entirely fair for all players. As its not really fair to point out something such as that without thinking it through yourself. Anyways. That's my review. Probably no one cares lol.

I like the concept alot. I enjoy going out and catching Pokémon. The only problem that I've found is that sometimes the game says "No WiFi Detected". It shouldn't need constant connection, especially since the point of Pokémon GO is to go outside and catch the Pokémon. I also kind of wish you could see other players avatars walking around if they were walking around in your area. Overall, I think it's a good game, but needs touches here and there. 4 stars.

Edit: this game has come a long way since it launched! I admit that i was not overly impressed at first but the continual updates and additions of more pokemon and activities have enhanced gameplay tenfold!!OP: It's just like Ingress, but with pokemon catching added in. I was hoping for an experience more like the games. Ingress is great and all, but it's not pokemon. We should have to fight the pokemon we try to catch. More character options regarding hairstyle would be great too.

Laggy and Ruined! I have been a player from day one, took about a year hiatus but came back because it seemed more user friendly. Found out recently some player have been able to use third party apps to get better Pokémon which is straight up cheating. And to make matters worse, they penalize players who play the game like Pokémon is supposed to be played by raising prices on already expensive necessities. Can't even be bothered to increase the amount you get for placing Pokémon on gyms! GREEDY!

There isn't really enough to do. Hunting Pokemon, going to PokeStops, and battling gyms gets somewhat repetitive & the rewards don't really get better (except for leveling up). Unlike a traditional game, I don't feel like I'm working towards anything. Update: knocking off 2 more stars because the developers refuse to fix bugs that are reported, or even admit that they're bugs in the first place.

Overall game is fun, but this review is to address the go fest. Really disappointed in this years fest. The price of the ticket is triple last years price, and the amount of content was far less. There were countless bugs that made it infuriating to play for many players, and the rate of shinies felt like they were far lower than previous year's go fest. A lot of people online are feeling ripped off by this annual event, and I really hope that Niantic addresses this in the coming weeks.

I loved this game when the tracker was working. I still like it, but losing the tracker took away some fun. I am really hoping a fix or something better will come in an update soon. I'm sticking with the game for now. I like to walk around and still catch Pokémon and battle gyms. Please keep this game fun and bring back some type of tracking system.

The game is great. But the storage system is absolutely annoying. My backpack is full, but yet I'm out of pokeballs. So I have to waste items by dumping them, making space for more balls. And then it takes forever to get coins from gyms to upgrade your bag. If you don't have a good Pokémon for the gym it takes even longer. And then 100 coins for 20 pokeballs. I would say it's not even worth spending.
the game keeps freezing when I try to select a new egg to hatch

Shame on you Niantic for changing the rules during a pandemic. Also, as someone with limited mobility, you've made it difficult for me to participate in the game by taking the extended location to a gym or pokestop away. I'm a level 40 player, started playing July 15th, 2016. I'm rethinking where I'll now spend my gaming dollars... all of the new changes make me not want to play anymore. 😭

Used to really enjoy the game, but Niantic has been slowly and methodically rolling back features that benefited players. The game used to reward legendary Pokémon simply for doing research tasks seven days in a row, now you're lucky if the Pokémon isn't actively spawning in the wild. Plus, the constant drive to increase prices for items in the shop practically force you to spend real money if you want to make any progress at all.

* They have changed the spawn locations so now they're everywhere around us, even in the middle of nowhere! * We're on a farm and it makes it tough to play. I wish they were still accepting Poke-Stop location recommendations. It's a great game, my kids (and i) love it, it just gets expensive buying everything all the time vs hitting stops. Also, they used to be able to atleast hit the stops while we were driving, now I have to stop the car and wait.

Edited*** Was a 5 star review. Was a whale, spending thousands over the last few years. But after some changes they announced today, I will be uninstalling. Biggest is increasing the price of fundamental in game items by double the previous price, and putting a limit. The items in question are remote raid passes, which are required if you want to raid with friends that are elsewhere, or just to fill your lobby as many raids need 4+ people. This will effectively destroy a main aspect of the game

Started out loving it,  but with all the pointless restrictions I've decided to quit. I'm not sure if they are being forced to add speed limit restrictions or if they just want to ruin the game for most people.  Either way it's no longer fun.  Even with walking around spawns suck unless you're in a city.  If you're in a city I'm sure you will find it enjoyable at least.

The updates are a constant bother. Lucky I gave you 1 star. Glad I'm not alone. This game was great but over the years of playing it's just got harder and harder unless you invest $$$ and that's just low. I was thinking on reinstall but after reading some of the most critical reviews not a chance! I've mentioned the battery issue just after it was released and still nothing done. That's a serious issue. Who wants to be charging there phone every five minutes? Shame on you money hungry monkeys.

This game has become to expensive. With the upcoming price increases and the limits they are implementing, make me not wanna play it any more. I live in a rural area and pokestops and gyms aren't close by, not to mention that there aren't that many players in my are so I rely on remote raids a lot. It's already expensive as it is but now they are increasing prices to almost double. Forget this game. It's not worth it.

Additions made due to the pandemic actually made the game better and more wide-ranging. However now Niantic wants people to go back in time to before the pandemic, when their game had a blossoming in person community. Those times are gone now. They have raised prices, made in store boxes garbage, and are trying to force players to go back to the way things were. They are now focusing attention on another IP & don't seem to care about the game that made them recognizable. Just a cash cow

The only thing this game has going for it is the Pokemon IP. There is literally nothing good about this game right now. It has potential, but there are currently only 2 ways to play this game. The first is to walk around aimlessly and hoping you get lucky going within 200m range of a rare Pokemon, and the second is to sit at a cluster of lures without moving. Neither is exciting. The nearby list needs to show rarer Pokemon at a longer range with more tools to track down the Pokemon.

I lost 20 lbs in 6 weeks due to walking an extra 50 km (31 miles) per week. It's great that this game promotes physical activity, gets people outside, and encourages people to socialize. However, the game has many bugs. I don't get 50 PC for having pokemon in a gym for a full day, there are times it says I lost when I actually won the battle, etc. There are also some game mechanics that I find ridiculous. Starter pokemon is obsolete, no control on pokemon's move set, etc.

The game is entertaining, if not all out buggy, but the game plays like the devs have never played a Pokemon game in their life. Then because the game is centered around physical locations, you can bet there are gonna be some events and special Pokemon you're going to miss out on. Random crashes, bugs, glitches and poorly planned events add up to a frustrating experience. Can be fun to play with friends for a while, when the weather is good, but I wouldn't recommend spending much money on it.

I love this game. I love the concept. I love the ambition. I want to give it 100 stars just for the shear nostalgic joy it brings me... However, without pvp real-time battles, trading of items/pokemon, and the repetitive options given geolocation, plus the complete lack of power balancing for a casual player compared to someone with not life and/or bots running. It's jut not what I was promised with the advertising and teasers. Years later they still are missing the mark. Prabably realized they can use slot machine tactics to rake in money for minimum effort. It's a shame Nintendo is letting their name get attached to something that's so against their normal way of running their business.

I've been four years without playing it and because the game seems more attractive now, I'm back. But Niantic isn't really trying to adapt it in regards to Covid-19 quarentine. You could at least give us a few pokeballs for logging in. I don't live next to a pokestop and because I can't get Cobalion as a Go Battle reward (0 pokeballs), I can't battle, either. Basically I can't play it and I'm pretty sure lots of people around the world are facing the same situation.

This game is a fun concept, and can be addictive. Its constant push you to go outside, which sounds great, but its not the reason they tell you. They also expect you to install your own pokestops in game, vote on others & use your camera to take videos of locations for them. What do you get in return? A bug filled, working-half-the-time game. After 3 years playing consistently & thousands of $ down the drain, I'm unstalling until the game let's me play the way I learned. Please sell the game.

While the game is one of the main things I play in my free time, it neglects areas with less of a playerbase. I can walk around for hours on end if not an entire day and not find a single shiny (even during events where the shinies are supposedly boosted). Meanwhile people who live in more populated areas can find tons of shinies each day with less effort. I'd give a higher rating if gameplay was improved in the areas with less players and not just ignored.

Game won't load. Can't play.~~~~~ Niantic has been putting out some really good content lately and it's really improved the game! Between research and making friends it's been a whole new experience! The above review is still valid, but now there are a lot of "Paid" additions. Shinys are stuck behind paywalls, and and there is a lot of Paid research. The revamped raids are awesome but I don't spend on raid passes so I only do one raid or 2 if im given a free raid pass.

I've been playing this game since it started. One of the few things I absolutely despise about it is the forced updates. Not all updates are forced, but some won't allow you to open the game until you update. Niantic doesn't listen to the patrons of the game. There are many others concerns they have yet to attempt to address. **update** As of 01-17-2024, there is an issue where my account won't "authenticate" and I have major problems logging in to play. No help from support after 3 days...

A little laggy at times, but overall pretty good. I do wish, however, that more uncommon and rare Pokemon (Unown for example) would pop up more frequently. Need to also add more Gyms and PokeStops for those that live in rural areas. Also, it would be really cool to be able to sort your pokemon according to how they're appraised (Amazing, Great, Good, etcc...) as well.

The game is fun and addictive and has given me and my son something to bond over :) The glitches and the lack of the 3 step map is annoying but we don't usually have a hard time finding the Pokémon.. The constant loss of GPS signal frustrates me too but... we still have fun! Update: 3-31-20 My son and I still play everyday and we LOVE IT! So many things to do - I have a hard time keeping up! Great job, Niantic!

Bought an Android phone and started playing right after release. At some point, Niantic changed my nickname by appending a "3" to the end, and allowed some random player to take the name for themselves. They refuse to fix their mistake even when provided proof that I did not change it, my account was not compromised, and that I am the original holder of the name. Fine game, bad customer service.

It seems a fun game, it brings me back to my childhood but it has a big flaw. In order for the pokemon to appear while you walk you have to be connected to a network which consumes lodes of data if you're without wifi network. After a first "test drive" on the streets in places where I was sure I had good internet connection the game crashed while catching pokemon, I lost the pokemon and the balls used on them. Please fix these bugs.

I really like this game and I've been playing it for sometime. However there are a few things I feel should be improved. The biggest is the amount of daily obtainable coins should definitely be bumped up a little. I mean I get this is a freemium game but the amount of coins you get per day compared to the cost of shop items is pretty pitiful. I just don't want this to turn into another Clash of Clans grind type game that seem to be everywhere is all.

The only game I like to play. Lots to do and fun But there are to many glitches and errors and lately the game has become automated, makes the experience feel less real. Which ultimately makes it just another game. A month ago it wasn't like that. Catching Pokémon in Raids are also a no go. You will get 1 out of every 5 battles. Gets expensive.

This game is just a money grab clearly. When it first launched I was ok with what little it had. The nostalgic quality was amazing. But now that I see them removing core features of the game, shutting down 3rd party sites, making Pokemon harder to catch, making spawn rates terrible.. what's the point in playing anymore especially when I can just easily hook into their API and catch all the Pokemon and take over all the gyms. I only play because it's something to do with my girlfriend.

The game is fun, but it is very frustrating how often it glitches. I noticed this more recently after the last update. Battles glitch. Catching pokemon.....glitch. Pokestops, glitch. And it is especially frustrating in the battles when you lose because of it and you don't get anything because it glitches. It says I lost when in fact I actually won. And no, this is not my phone or my wifi.

I am absolutely obsessed with this game and I have been playing everyday for almost 6 months now. And even more recently! I love it I just have a couple requests. I think we need more revives in pokestops. OR there needs to be some sort of healing period. Because there are pokemon I will probably never revive because they're so low and I have almost 200 or more in the revive column and only ever have like 5 revives at a time and they're too expensive to buy that many one day I bought like 12-15 and that was like $10 and still wasn't enough. I also want to know why now that it has switched back to the original pokemon why they are all so low CP? Are they just not that great of pokemon? Like everything I've caught is around 200 and everything I was catching before was 500- 1000s. Idk if it's a glitch or what but it bums me out. I've been waiting for alot of these character's to come back so I can finish them or to level up higher and that is proving to be difficult with the low cps. Thank you for such an amazing game. I am so absolutely impressed. And will probably play as long as theres new stuff to do. I also loved the idea of the quests. Great way to re-energize the game. I love everything just a couple of thoughts. Thank you!

Every time I see a pokemon I get close but it never pops up and when I go somewhere else it disappears so I know its in that one spot but it doesn't show up this is really stupid. It would also be nice if you could make this game compatible for Samsung Galaxy S3. I wish there was an option to switch between teams whenever you wanted and be able to pick up the pokeballs that miss the pokemon or bounce off of it. I really hope can do world trading.

As a huge Pokemon fan I was super excited for this and as far as gameplay goes it's not bad. However, they really don't have any accommodation for folks with disabilities. I can't leave the house most days due to physical limitations, so there's no way to get pokestops, combat gyms, earn coins, or complete challenges of capture. It makes me feel really left out as a pokemon lover.

The gym battle mechanics is ulterly broken. All gym battles basically takes three tries to take down the gym. A buddy and I fought two of them ourselves. On the final attempt, another player joined. For some reason, that other player from different team were given priority to add Pokemon to the gym. And gyms areich easier to defend than attack, even 2:1. It's crazy frustrating. I uninstalled the game right there.

So far so good. The graphics and gameplay, though simple, is surely addicting and enjoyable. It lags some of the time maybe because of my mobile connection. Im waiting for the new tacking system and the IV calculator. I am also looking forward for the 2nd generation pokemon to come out. Keep it up Niantic! 1/8/2021 I am trying to get back to the game when I heard you can now level up to 50. Its still fun, more tasks and things to do. But why do I feel like this has been a pay to win game?

It is a real shame that Niantic is ok with watching this game go up in flames. The release was blocky, but that was to be expected. Then they added in bugs. Yes, they knowingly added in bugs to their own game. They never voice anything to the players on their direction of the game. Their "updates" only seem to make the game worse as well. Players no longer can play the game as it was intended. People in small towns get essentially punished and do not have the capabilities as people who live in big cities.

It's awful. They took anything and everything that was good about the Pokemon games and just left it out. This game is a shameless cashgrab with broken loot game style mechanics. The battle system is absolute trash. The only good thing to say about the game is you can catch just about everything. Shinies are easier to get. Then you can send them to Pokemon home and other games. Every other aspect of the game is one giant microtransaction. I'd rather have paid full price for a real Pokemon game.

Great game and pioneer in AR technology. I rated it 4 stars based on its potential of being a great game in the future. I Love the concept of bringing gamers out to parks and making them cooperate in a battle (i.e. legendary raids). For now, several features such as battle gameplay, pvp, and pokemon development (training, breeding) are either missing or must be improved. It could bring more gamers in if we can add more tactical depth in combat rather than just making them tap to death. Besides, this can make people give up on having multiple accounts without the counter-productive ban waves. 😉

They had PokeVision taken down. That was the only way to locate a Pokemon seeing as they can't fix the tracker. Unless you live in the city, you can expect to find mostly pidgy or rattata. Unless you are in a area with many pokestops nearby, you'll have to spend money on pokeballs. Expect to waste most of them because the pokemon can run away, dodge the ball, and jump out. So, for a game that suppose to inspire you to get out and explore, it becomes very uninspiring quickly. I hope they make it fun somehow.

I love this game overall but there are a few issues they should fix and some things I would love to see added. One is you run out of pokeballs so easily, especially if you don't live in an area with many pokestops. So I think they should have a daily reward. Second, the servers are actually getting quite better but they still crash. Third, I think it would be amazing if you can either assemble your own team with other players or battle against other players you bump into. Love this game, keep it up👍 Edit (2 years later) - I got back into it and I'm completely addicted again. The game is way better than when it first came out and I can not stop playing.

The game is great in general but I've found a few fundamental issues with trading that could be improved. There is no warning in game that you cannot trade back your Pokémon, therefore causing me to lose one of my best ones when attempting to get a lucky Pokémon. This is poor game design and user experience. This could be solved by allowing trade backs, with possibly a cool down of 30 days so as to not take advantage. Also needs a popup warning before confirming trade.

I enjoy it a lot, with every few months there is more Pokemon added to catch. The only reason I do not give it five stars is because of walking. Unless you have unlimited data, you used a lot of data trying to catch Pokemon or hatching eggs. And it does not count my steps if I do not have the game on while I am walking, even with it being synced. I would love it could connect to some kind of fitness bracelet or device that counts the steps without the use of data

I live in a rural area and have had this game since 2018. I never really got into it until this past February when I learned how remote raids work. Less than 2 months later, Niantic has doubled the price of remote raids and told us it's bad for the game. I know it is bad timing for me, but they essentially shut down the one thing I've ever found fun about this game, as soon as I found it. Would not recommend, even for pokemon fans.

Since having upgraded their servers, networks etc and the average userbase has better phones/connections in the two years since the game's release, Pokemon Go has genuinely become a playable experience. The trouble, however, is that even despite the game functioning well (FINALLY), it still just sucks as a pokemon title. Truth. Niantic took the lazy route and made no effort to make it feel like a pokemon game. Its a cash grab and nothing more. I cant even recommend it is a fitness app. Two years since release and it still has basically zero gameplay. Meanwhile, my pokemon yellow cartridge from what, 1999? Is still playable and has a bit of gameplay left to be absorbed. Just really sad to see this multi million dollar endeavor fall so far short of its potential, and yet somehow people are still putting money into it. Shame.

It's not fun having to travel place to place to catch a certain pokemon, especially if you're limited on traveling. It was a cool idea but it made me realise that some people can't play because of that. Also no matter how much you change it, the battle system just doesn't work for the game. This is the reason why you see so many spoofers. No one wants to play a game where you have to go to mexico just to catch a latias or something. I can just open pokemon ruby and catch more pokemon in 10 mins.

Pretty good game, but for people who don't want to spend money right now it's not great, although that's mainly location-wise. If you live in a smaller town, or outside of one, you can't do much. I'd have to walk over a mile for the nearest pokestop or gym, and I can't get pokeballs otherwise, unless there is a free gift. I like the game, but I can only play occasionally or else I'll have no pokeballs and nothing to do.

Its been several years so I thought I would update my review. This game is a solid time waster, but with no redeeming gameplay aspects. I feel more like I'm doing chores trying to play catch up on collecting the hordes of useless pokemon in search of the 1/1000+ decent spawns. Lots of new features added, but the core of the series still isn't present, years later.

It's $9.99 for about 1200 coins and after you buy coins you can buy items that you pretty much need if you want to progress in the game. Items such as Pokeballs, Potions, they even charge you for extra storage space which you'll need if you wanna "Catch'em all". So now after spending $10 for 1200 coins you can shop but you won't get much. It's 200 for 40 Pokeballs or 450 for 100 Pokeballs, 200 for 50 extra Pokemon storage space, another 200 for extra items space. Niantic is a crooked company.

I mean its a great concept and it's certainly fun when you are active and have friends...otherwise, it gets old fast and bored me pretty quickly. I have probably uninstalled it three times just because I get bored of it. It seems like more work to level up Pokemon and way too costly, especially if you aren't Gym level yet, since you don't get the option to actually get experience by batting other Pokemon. That was half the fun of Pokemon. But no, you just run into one...and catch it. No real skill required. Seems more like a trading card kind of collecting than actually leveling your Pokemon and earning it.

This app has done so much in such a small amount of time. It's addictive, encourages going outside to see your surroundings and view various landmarks. People come together and friends are made through common interest of Pokémon. On the downside with the removal of the tracking feature and banning of 3rd party sites/apps, it's just a blind walk in the dark finding Pokémon. They run away much more often and the game fails to locate gps sometimes.

An edit of my review since 2016: Thanks for the countless extra Pokéstops and gyms. Helps to make me more active again. I wish I could capture higher level CP Pokémon, but I understand; my level is, as of writing, only 20. I like the different missions to get extra stuff and the variety of Pokémon depending on the weather. (And the extra stats). So yeah, guess I'm back on the grind (though I wish there were less needed microtransactions...)

Niantic actively makes it harder for people to play the game by pushing in person play features and making it harder to play remotely (less incense spawns when stationary, remote raid pass prices going up). If you live in a rural environment, are disabled, or even if there's really bad/dangerous weather outside, you can't play at all. This does not make for an inclusive game and overall the changes push people away rather than bring them together.

Its pokemon, you know what to expect. I've been playing for over 5 years. Changing my 5 star review from 5 years ago to a 1 star due to negligent handling of the game and unnecessary price gouging. The chances of catching a legendary are so low as is, spending money on remote raid passes is not a guarantee to get anything in return and they've doubled the cost of them. While not perfect, raid passes made the game playable for so many. I won't be back until they've made things better.

This game has so much potential but is ultimately a pay to win game, meaning, if you don't have perfect 5g internet you will lose your battles all the time. I don't know why they went away from the traditional battle type where it was turn based. Even more frustrating, when you are "rewarded" for doing well in trainer battles and are forced to catch very difficult Pokemon you don't even want, it makes me want to uninstall. I worked hard to get pokeballs and then the game forced me to use them.

Ever since recent updates. "Max raids" and so forth. The game doesn't feel like a pokemon game. To find pokemon, you have to "technically" dig through a haystack to find the needle. When this game first came out, there was an abundance of pokemon, both regular and legendary. Including shinies. This game has been in decline for the past 4 years, and still Niantic refuses to do anything about it. This game is not worth it. It takes too much time for so little enjoyment or completion.

They have made some positive changes but it's still very difficult to play this game in a rural setting. Getting good pokemon, making money, etc. seems to rely solely on access to gyms and pokestops which basically exist only in populated areas. Not going anywhere for a couple days results in the game becoming unplayable. You run out of all resources and the only way to get more is to pay through the nose for pokecoin. I would love this game if they'd make it more accessible.

As a long time Pokémon fan, I loved this game. It had a ton of problems out the gate but I gave it a chance. After the most recent update, the devs have removed tracking pokemon from the game, which is kind of the whole idea. Without the option to track Pokémon, the game is pointless and boring. Something that I used to go out to play is now something that I only occasionally play when I'm already out. I'm confident that the game will lose users fast if changes aren't made soon and the company communicates.

This app used to be great until they destroyed the radar. They removed the ability to actively track Pokemon and basically made a game of luck in the real world. So now instead of actually taking the time, having skill and exploring around, you are essentially gambling with your health walking into traffic because good luck trying to find what you're looking for. Now with the reduced spawn rates in a system where 40 million exp is the difference between two levels at the very end, is ridiculous.

Five years and you guys still can't manage to make a bug free event quest? You guys have about reached the extent of what riding on the coat tails of a multi-billion dollar franchise can get you, I think, and your true capabilities and colors are beginning to show. Absolutely talentless and worthless. It was a good run, but if you're thinking about just getting into the game at this point, just put it down and play an actual Pokemon game instead of this five year, classless cash grab.

Although the game started out as addicting, due to constant issues and poor update decisions, you can only basically log in to hatch eggs, hit up pokestops, and catch whatever pops up. There's no way to really have any control in the game - like hunting for specific pokemon in your area, throwing the ball, or even catching the pokemon. (Let's be real, a 10cp pokemon should never be able to run away...). That said. Still hopeful.

Editing my review due to changes put in place by Niantic over the last year. Can no longer recommend this game to anyone who hasn't already been playing for years, unless you have hundreds of dollars to spend on it, hours each day to walk to and around only highly active play areas, and a local community to play with. New players will. Not have a good time trying to catch up.

I've played this since it was released officially in the UK. Since then, it's gained so many features that are fundamental to Pokemon, that it is essentially a fully fledged Pokemon game in its own right, rather than a quick money grabber. It occasionally suffers reliability issues but those tend to get resolved soon after, and it's adapted well to lockdown measures from COVID. Overall, if you like Pokémon, there's no reason to miss out on playing this.

I've been a dedicated Pokémon Go player for years, but the recent price increase of Remote Raid Passes is really disappointing. These passes were a great way to stay connected with friends and participate in raids from anywhere, especially during the pandemic. Now, with the higher prices, it feels like the game is becoming less accessible for many players. I hope Niantic reconsiders this decision and makes the game more affordable again!

I have been locked out of my game for days. It asked if it was a real player. I can't answer; I'm locked out. My app nickname is Suppashiz, and they've came in contact many times, and I've made purchases. I started at the end of Aug. I'm not any good, but I've never played another game. Things are better and whener problems occur, they are quickly addressed.

I've been playing this a lot, while partaking in my daily walks out and about the neighborhood. I've not been a Pokefan much in the past but really feel like this game rewards you for getting out and doing some exercise. Like the Ingress game it's based on, there's strategic locations around your neighborhood you can visit to find resources, that you can use to capture Pokémon and to improve the ones you have. You don't have to fight other people if you don't want to either, which is nice.

Playing on a galaxy s6 active. The game works well, it froze a lot the first few days I played but they've worked out some kinks in the servers, and I haven't had problems since. It does drain my battery, but nothing a portable charger can't fix (bought a cheap one at '5 Below' with no troubles). It uses very little data, for the most part. As long as you have a newer phone, this game should work great for you :) I've loved it so far.

Two features that this game needs. 1.) You should be able to spin any pokestop, no matter how far away you are from it, as long as you have a Pokemon in that gym. 2.) Item trading/trading Pokemon for items. Some of the items are really hard to get and considering they are necessary to complete the pokedex, like the Sinnoh and Unova Stone, item trading would be a welcome addition to this game that, while developing slowly, has developed into a pretty good game all around.

I have played this game religiously since day one. Once covid hit, they updated and implemented remote raids. It was exciting getting to play with friends all over the world, and overall made this game so much more exciting to keep playing. However, due to niantics decision to continue to up the *already* expensive price of remote passes amung other things, I can not continue to play this game. Niantic has proved they are just money hungry. Fix your bugs and get rid of the outrageous prices.

It's a fun, annoying game. There is always something different happening. I do believe in order to catch "rare" or "cool" pokemon should be more of an option. It deffinitly is a game to get you outside, walking and moving while having fun. As someone who knows absolutely nothing about pokemon, I do enjoy this game and it definitely has the ability to continue growing to be better.

Great game if you have like 5 or 6 friends nearby to play with. Right now you don't even have to be close, just coordinate yourselves. It would be nice to communicate within the game tho. There's people i got on my friend list that i only know from there, and sometimes i would like to send a message like "raid in 10min" or something similar.

Updated review 2 years later: with all the additions and updates, the game is a lot better! I enjoy all the new features, including raids, items, missions, and trading. I do wish that the walking feature could read my steps when I'm not actively using the app, that the app wasn't draining my battery, and that there was more types of Pokemon were strong enough for gyms. This game is really addicting and it is fun collecting Pokémon. However if it weren't for the Pokémon, I would've uninstalled this game a long time ago. Multiple issues like freezing, server/logging in, broken tracker, lack of real battling or trading, etc makes this a highly unfinished and buggy game. Great idea and potential, poor execution

Niantic continues to disappoint by being themselves. No reason for Go Fest tickets to cost so much, they barely develop new content at all. Most "content" we get these days is in the form of research missions, which hardly ever require new assets. And that's fine, this game is what it is, but there's no reason to charge up the arse for something that doesn't take much to maintain at all.

The gameplay is decent, but don't waste your money. There is no customer satisfaction, they only take with no user support. The problem is with the support, it is "unfortunately" very poor. They will not address issues or try to help you out. I have had several problems with raiding, and my towns local gyms. They have had "network" issues for a month and a half. "unfortunately" they have no timeline or fix at this time.

everything is fine, except for the fact that nothing of what you purchase in-game (for example, a backpack for extra space) does not apply to your account ever. NOT TO MENTION it will NOT track your steps if your phone/the app is not open. you have to keep your phone on the app, without turning it off, for it to ever count. it's a battery waster. plus, ever since another company bought this app, the gyms don't work. the app will freeze if you try to enter one, forcing you to close and reopen it.

Still having sign in issues. For the last 2 days the game would load or let me in. So I finally gave up and signed out to try and sign back in but forgot my password so now I have to go through that whole process again! That's my biggest issue with this game. I have it set to automatically sign me in and run the game but when it stops loading, I am basically forced out of the game. How has this problem not been fixed yet?

I am a huge fan of pokemon, ever since I was in grade school. Have a lot of memories playing the games, trading and sometimes battling. So when I found out that there was a Pokemon app, I was ecstatic. However the concept of the game is simply beautiful and it is fun to play, bringing back memories of my youth, it tends to crash a lot. Or runs terribly slow. It'll freeze after a battle or even after I catch a Pokemon. I would love for a smoother game. Till then, I only give 3 stars.

This is an alright app. Basically, just something to do if you are bored. Leveling up yourself and your Pokemon is a difficult challenge, especially if you live in the country. Additionally, the amount of candies it takes to evolve Pokemon is absurd, especially for Magikarp. For me, I rarely see any Pokemon besides the extremely common ones, and I have enough of those. This app could be improved up immensely.

I'm an OG Pokemon Go player from launch day. I'm sure a lot of people were like me and after sometime, when they broke the game by messing up pokestops and the nearby tracker, they stopped playing. But I've recently returned hearing of all thenewchsnges, and I have to say I'm hooked again! They did a great job fixing a lot of the bugs and I love all of the new features. They made it to where you -can- play at home, but are more rewarded byventuring out into the world and hunting. I'm glad that they kept that in the game. To me, that's what gave this game most if not all of itschsrm. The possibility of going out and bumping into other people playing, which I still do today!

Overall, Pokemon go is a fairly good game. I have been playing for a little while and have noticed a few things. While it is very fun to collect Pokemon, look for shiniest, etc., events such as Go Fest obviously favoring certain areas is incredibly annoying. Is it our fault for not living there? Also, pvp is incredibly broken with lag and delay making the game almost unplayable. Overall, pretty good.

Good Game, but has some issues which have taken me to write this review. First, the distribution of poke stops and gyms throughout the land is truly bad for those that live in villages or less crowded areas. I understand that makes more sense to have more where are more players, but try to spread some interesting spots each Km. Secondly, remove the limitation of 50 coins for the first day at a gym. Took over a gym in my village and haven't been able to neither get my pkmn back or get coins.

Loved it when it first came out despite all the server issues. Now Niantic is proving to be a terrible company by ignoring everyone and fighting against 3rd party resources (who are just trying to fill in the gaps where Pokémon Go is unable to). It's still fun to casually use the app, but the passion is sapped out of the game play because of Niantic's antics. The main feature I'm referring to is tracking nearby Pokémon. Tons of other bugs and problems too, but that one killed the passion really.

I have fun playing this game as a means of motivation for getting outdoors and catching cute and cool Pokemon, but it seems as though every new major update lessens quality of life, and the developers could care less about their playerbase. If you're alright with not being heard as a community and can live with continuous downgrades, then give the game a go! Be prepared to "learn to live with it," though, almost every time they push something new.

Do not waste your time!!!! Was excited to play, but game is only good if you live in a massive metropolis. If ess than 500k people in your city it is a dead game unless you want to dump tons of money into it. Better free to play games out there that actually make you want to play. Pokestops are the only viable way to get items, but if you live in a small town (I live in one with a per Capita of 2000/square mile) you won't be able to actually keep enough items to play regularly. Uninstalled!!!!

Updated March 2023. Game is all about the money! More specifically the money you spend. Been playing since July 2016 and play less now than ever before. L50 player the hard way. Game has become a money machine for Niantic. Ridiculous! And if you don't spend money you don't catch shinys or get special releases...like the latest must have a $200 + game to catch new releases to PoGo. Game has gotten boring enough that I don't need to waste money on a new console game to get new releases.

After the most recent price hike, the game truly isn't worth all the time and effort anymore. The game is plagued by glitches and errors with AR being pushed heavily, while being implemented poorly. With taking over gyms, at most recieve 50 coins, even if your stay is 5+days which doesn't make sense. And, with the increased cost for raid passes and in game features, it spoils the purpose of the game. General gameplay shouldn't be hidden behind a pay wall. Niantic has truly failed the community.

Update: Some things I love, and some things I don't like. I wish I could give it both four stars, and one star simultaneously. Here's the thing- I've been playing this game on and off since the beginning. Boxes are way expensive for less product. Incense don't work well, and Pkmn flee all of the time. Even with excellent throws/berries. Pkmn we saw in the beginning are impossible to get now. 50 pk coin limit, which is awful. Not disabled friendly. Lost free remote raid pass. They just want $.

Oof. The reduced reach distance is really impacting the gameplay. We're supposed to avoid crowded spaces and yet at the same time get right on top of each pokestop? So many pokestops and gyms are in the middle of buildings or in private places, and are now yet again unreachable. My other complaint- outside of events, we get the same 10 pokemon appear in the wild and that's it. No more surprise of stumbling into something rare... I don't feel motivated to explore anymore when it's all the same.

screw what i said before. this game is amazing. My past review for this game was 5 stars. And with each update they've released it's gotten lower for me. The game has some of the same bugs in it since launch, they continue to add the most pointless features to the game instead of giving players what they ask for. I don't understand niantic's decision making on some things but oh well. I'm quitting that game now that I've reached level 25 and maybe I'll try it again in a few months.... Or not

I have been waiting for this game for 20 years. Yes, it has bugs, but those can be fixed and I hope Niantic gets these messages and fixes the problem. I wish there were more items given away, instead of just for leveling up. Give daily rewards to keep people playing. Give rewards for those badges you get for walking a certain distance or catching a number of certain types of Pokemon. Give more items instead of relying on store purchases. I love this game and will play it as long as it improves

I've been playing this game since it came out and I love it. I have made many successful in app purchases until yesterday. Yesterday i bought $9.99 (1200 pokecoins) and didnt the coins, contacted niantic for them to say nothing they can do doesn't show that i paid it even though i sent a screen shot of the receipt. Three times. Beware. *Update (i forgot to but better late than never) so niantic never fixed the problem google ended up fixing it for me even though the error was on niantics side.

You know, I was really excited when I played this game at the beginning of this year. Until recent, I re-downloaded it so my Husband and I can play together. Everything was great up until the point where the App was not registering my location (GPS) and him next to me, was registering. Overall, this App/game is Amazing, I would of given it a Five Star if it wasn't for the small issues.

Editing my previous review. Graphics are great. It's repetitive and grind focused as any Pokemon game. They never learn to improve the play experience.1thing that bugs me is the need to catch multiple pokemon over and over and over of the same type going through a gazillion animations. Too many animations for a grind game..learn to make games less grindy!! Gets boring over time. Bad weather affects your ability to play it as well. Average game.

Its ok. Just ok. Yes it's fun, but we're limited by the constant bugs (even on flagship high end phones) and the features we all expected, and wanted in the gameboy versions that are not available on PkMnGo. While yes this IS a different game entirely, it could of started with trading, and from the very first commercial for PkMnGo we were promised battles (what looked like PvP) which still has not happened. The release of each generation slowly over time is a good idea, but the concept that everyone can get every legendary when the gameboy games made this near-impossible at times, is lame. If everyone has a legendarily then they aren't really something amazing and rare anymore.  In short: Its a good game to play while you're on a walk some place.

When, not if, there's a problem that involves using support, prepare to be gaslighted and ignored. They take no suggestions for improvement, they refuse to compensate items when things are clearly their fault, and they'll outright lie to players on game mechanics and anything else they can. Stay far away from this garbage. Niantic is an absolute stain on the Pokémon franchise. I could go on about other issues, but I only have 500 characters to use even though an entire novel wouldn't be enough.

Niantic goes out of their way to try and force you to play the game the way they intended and not the way the player may wish to interact with it. They have taken what was once a good game and through a series of close minded moves and complete lack of listening to the player base turned it into a barely playable mess. If you're disabled and can't go outside stay far away because you will not enjoy this stain on the Pokemon license. Same if you live in a rural area.

Ball throwing bug has been fixed! Overall, PoGo is pretty good these days. Lots to do and lots of events. For QoL improvement, I'd like to see 2 separate pages for "Nearby" & "Sightings" so it's easier to see close PokéMon that aren't at a PokéStop. It'd also be nice if there was more than one of a specific type of PokéMon nearby, that they'd only show in one spot with a number of how many there are in the icon. Like, "Rattata (x3)"

Ever since I took the update, I was forced to take to be able to continue playing the game, Pokémon run away almost every time and take 5 or more poké balls to try to catch a Pokémon. Even after feeding them fruit they still run away. Whatever glitch you guys added to the game to make Pokémon almost uncatchable needs to be fixed. The game is becoming no fun due to not being able to ever catch the critters. :( This game has become horrible. FIX YOUR BUGS!!!!

I've played this game since it first came out. In many ways it has drastically improved since 2016! They've introduced trading, buddy pokemon, a friends list and PvP battliing. Unfortunately with each step forward, it feels like we also take 2 steps back. With each QoL update that we've gotten, Niantic have found new ways to nickle and dime the players. I'm slowly starting to feel like I'm being priced out of the game. Niantic as a company seems to be very unresponsive to player feedback.

The game had so much potential but there are game breaking bugs in every aspect of the game. Want to power up your Pokemon's CP? Error. Want to fight at this gym? You can take the opponent to 1hp then the game continues to run, but no actions are registered. Want to click on a Pokemon you found? Too bad you must have missed it, keep clicking. I wont be installing this game again. Dissapointing.

It's a shame, this game had so much potential. Events happen all the time, making catching Pokemon in natural nests or biomes difficult. The trainer battle addition is bland. I have a decent record of 60 wins, 40 loses, so this is not just coming from someone who always loses. Gym battles don't feel rewarding anymore since the rewards for holding gyms depend on you getting booted from said gym. So you can hold a gym for 2 weeks and never see a return on your effort. Game is a big cash grab.

This games amazing! There are some things that frustrate me... I feel like there should be a "Watch an add for 3 pokeballs!" thing, because it sucks when you run out and don't have any extra money to buy more, for example, I got really upset because a pokemon I really wanted popped up, but I had already used all my balls on other pokemon, and I couldn't buy more. I do understand that you get poke balls when you level up, but that'll take awhile

I Love it but as a newer player I'm having some difficulty learning certain aspects. Besides the TAGS (which I wish had more character space). I am currently limited on my walking so I try walking @ the house to find Pokemon. Sometimes I can get 1 or 2; other times it'll take hours before 1 popping up. Also wish there was a way to get more "Revive" items w/o paying. I kinda sometimes think there are too many categories of Pokemon. I have high CP 'Normal' Pokemon that never battle well.

Been playing since 2016 and as of recently have been struggling to bring myself to play. There are way too many limitations and caps for even the most simple of things. Can't open more than 20 gifts in one day, can't do more than 5 remote raids a day, can't do more than 25 online battles a day. I don't know if the developers just hate it when people are having fun, but the game has become so time gated I can't do half the things I want without being told "come back tomorrow". Very unfortunate.

Developers: I would have given this game a 5 star rating, until I realized that Tsam Rocket gets unlimited shields in battle, and I only get 2. How is this fair? I downloaded this when it first came out, and loved it. Unfortunately, I'm going to be uninstalling, Devs skewed this game to make money, and I am catching the same pokemon over and over again. It's no fun anymore. The Devs are trying to catch more money, disguised as a game where we try to catch Pokemon.

It's a pretty fun game. It's just that sometimes when I open it and it's loading, it never finishes loading so I have to close and reopen the app a few times. Also as of recent, the whole game becomes very slow after a while of having it open, like 2 minutes. Everything lags and looks horrible, resulting in everything taking much longer than normal. But this is just fixed by re-opening the app, which gets annoying quick. Otherwise, it's pretty fun and would be scored higher.

If you care about how your avatar gets to look, don't even bother playing or buying anything to customize it. The most recent update Niantic pushed out "updated" the models to look like an ugly mess. Now, no matter what you want to wear, you still look ridiculous. Even outside of this, any extra content that you might want to do is locked behind paywall after paywall. This game just isn't worth getting into at this point, steer clear.

It's much better than it was at launch, with a ton of things to do, trainers to battle, pokés to hatch. But you're screwed if you don't find a large, active community in your town. You NEED people for endgame content. Not only that, but there are still issues which Niantic won't address - like updating existing PokéStops/Gyms, adding new ones etc.

It's a good game at its core, but I recommend staying away from the in-app purchases at all costs. It really isn't worth it. Niantic continues to charge more for less, and changes implemented over time continue to show where their true focus lies. To Niantic, it's never about making the game more enjoyable and more about squeezing money out of the players. It really sours the experience.

UpdaThe point of this app is, at its heart, is hunting Pokemon. However, the developer has disabled any 'in app' means of actually hunting them down before they despawn. In addition, they've now disabled 3rd party apps that assisted with trying to make up for the bugs in the app. No communication from Niantic has only compounded these issues. This probably isn't as big an issue in large cities where rarer pokemon are everywhere. However, one star until I can actually hunt Pokemon again in my rural area.

Catching, collecting, and raiding is enjoyable, but they seem to focus more on gimmicks and costumes over adding more Pokémon. If you don't live in a big active city, don't expect much to do. PvP battling is also very poorly balanced and is nothing like traditional pokemon games. If you're looking to catch pokemon and have something to do while out walking, I'd recommend it. If you're looking for a mobile pokemon game where you can train and battle, don't bother.

Been playing this game since it was launched. I still say it is a fantastic game to play. Looking forward to be able to suggest changes for Gyms and Stops in the game, which I hope will be soon! A handful of Gyms I have come across are dangerously close to high traffic areas with 50mph speed limits, so would like to be able to alert Niantic and get them changed.

Wasted potential. It has been many months after release and we still don't have half of the features that were advertised in the trailers before release (like trading and legendary pokemon battle). What's worse is that this game was a global phenomenon and didn't keep players happy by adding things to the game. Instead, we got months of silence and small to miniscule updates. Edit: took them two years but the game has finally improved. Still has a long way to go to get to where it should be.

Great game for all pokemon lovers. New update and trying to reinstall on 4/25/20 and it won't install. Just keep getting the waiting for download circle of death. 🙁 Cleared the cache on Google play and it fixed the issue. First time this happened since I started playing. Battle league is a joke. Gives you a group of Pokemon best for the upcoming match and they're not. They're not even close to being the ' best ' and your opponent can do multiple attacks some how. Waste of time.

Lately this game has been unplayable. Used to be I'd crash one to three times a day, now it's somewhere close to 50. It took me two mossy lures and two hours to catch just 10 pokemon, and kept losing spawned pokemon I needed for a collection to yet another crash. Last week I totally lost out on the chance to catch Tapu Bulu after a successful raid because I crashed. AGAIN. There's not enough room in this box to address my list of complaints. Sucks to spend money on a game you can't play.

Basically it's like one of those pet collecting games but with AR and Pokémon. The game really only focuses on collecting Pokémon and trading them. There are some combat mechanics but it really leaves a lot to be wanted. There's not really much you can do with your Pokémon, trade or use them to fight which doesn't do much to them really. The game lacks a clear direction and just follows a more pokemon is better mentality without ever fixing gameplay mechanics or adding needed ones. Plus BUGS!

been playing since release, the game has come to a point where it's just.. not as much fun as it used to be. microtransactions rule gameplay, they've become significantly more expensive and less rewarding. so many bugs, so many issues, so many great updates that were taken away. good luck if you're a rural player or disabled, it seems Niantic doesn't care about making their game playable & accessible to everyone, they only care about location data and money! #HearUsNiantic

Stepped away after being frustrated at the lack of spawns and ability to track spawn locations. Came back some years later and the game feels much better! Lots to do, doesn't feel pay-to-win (unless maybe you were in a remote area) and overall is a fun game to kill some time through the day. Lots of events and reasons to play those events is always a bonus. Can't think of any issues wild enough to dock a full star, but there's some minor ones here and there. TLDR; game good, download it.

If any other company had taken time to develop the game, it may have not ended as it is right now. Even current players love the game for what it could become, not what it is. So many missing features and so many missed opportunities offered from the community. It all depends on if Niantic can listen to the players. Edit: Aug/6/2021, I guess they don't listen to their player base. Been playing since 2016 and I finally uninstalled. Time to take a breather and live a little. It's been fun trainers

Server has issues but with every popular release there are server issues. The interface is easy to use. The fact you can get store items in game from PokeStops is even better! That was an extra plus i did not expect. Could use a better tutorial and explain significance of XS and XL pokemon. I'm expecting more social features to be added. Once those are in 5 stars all the way! Edited to 5 stars since they added friends.

Changing my review from 2016. Things are way different now. My biggest issue with the game now is storage space. I've spent more money on this game than any game I've ever played.
